definition_zh: 休眠；休眠状态；（行业等的）停滞期
definition_en: a temporary state in which growth, development or activity almost stops and resumes when conditions improve
core_image: 一只上了锁的抽屉里放着一粒种子和一只芽，抽屉外的季节轮转，抽屉里一切暂停
scene: 干土里，一粒种子把外壳收紧，内部的代谢慢到几乎测不出，等到雨水渗下来才重新吸水。 Deep dormancy keeps the seeds viable for years in dry soil.
sceneCN: 这里 dormancy 指「生长与代谢近乎停止、条件改善后可恢复的状态」（第 1 个义项：生物休眠状态）；句意为深度休眠使这些种子在干燥土壤中多年仍有活力。图中可辨识物件：土粒、种皮、滴落的水、细小的胚根。

pos.zh: 休眠；休眠状态；休眠期

derivatives.zh: 安息；被称为安眠的死亡

senses.title: Suspended growth or activity
senses.titleCN: 生长与活动近乎停止的状态
senses.definition: a temporary condition in which an organism's growth or metabolism slows almost to a stop and later resumes
senses.definitionCN: 生物的生长或代谢几乎停止、之后又能恢复的暂时状态
senses.example: Deep dormancy keeps the seeds viable for years in dry soil.
senses.exampleCN: 深度休眠使这些种子在干燥土壤中多年仍有活力。
senses.why: Latin dormire meant 'to sleep', so dormancy is the noun of a sleeping body, applied to seeds and spores that show no movement.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 dormire 意为「睡」，因此 dormancy 是「睡着的身体」的名词，用于看不出动静的种子与孢子。

senses.title: The period of suspended life
senses.definition: the interval between entering dormancy and the trigger that ends it
senses.definitionCN: 从进入休眠到触发其结束之间的间隔
senses.example: The dormancy of these acorns lasts until the first wet autumn.
senses.exampleCN: 这些橡子的休眠持续到第一个多雨的秋天。
senses.why: The noun can measure time as well as name a state, because dormancy is defined by its duration.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词既能量时间也能命名状态，因为休眠正是由持续时长来界定的。

senses.title: Seed dormancy
senses.definition: the condition in which a ripe seed will not germinate even with water and warmth until cold, light or time breaks the block
senses.definitionCN: 成熟的种子即使有水有温度也不萌发，须经低温、光照或时间才解除阻断的状态
senses.example: Seed dormancy spreads germination across several seasons instead of one week.
senses.exampleCN: 种子休眠把萌发分散到几个季节，而不是挤在一周内。
senses.why: A seed that waited for the right season would die in a false spring, so the block is a safety device.
senses.whyCN: 若种子在假春天萌发就会死去，因此这道阻断是一重保险。

senses.title: Bud and tuber dormancy
senses.definition: the winter or storage rest in which buds, tubers and bulbs will not sprout until chilling or warmth releases them
senses.definitionCN: 芽、块茎与球茎在冬季或储藏期不发芽，直到低温或回暖解除的状态
senses.example: Potato dormancy is broken by storing the tubers in cool, bright conditions.
senses.exampleCN: 把块茎放在凉爽明亮的环境中即可打破马铃薯的休眠。
senses.why: Here the sleeper is a bud rather than a whole plant, but the same rule holds: no growth until the signal arrives.
senses.whyCN: 这里睡着的是芽而非整株植物，但规则相同：信号不到就不生长。

senses.title: Bacterial and spore dormancy
senses.definition: the extremely low-activity state of spores and dormant bacteria, which can revive after long storage
senses.definitionCN: 孢子与休眠细菌活动极低、经长期存放仍可复苏的状态
senses.example: Spore dormancy can outlast the laboratory that first described it.
senses.exampleCN: 孢子的休眠可以比最初描述它的实验室活得更久。
senses.why: At this scale dormancy means a toughened coat and a nearly stopped metabolism, not sleep in any animal sense.
senses.whyCN: 在这个尺度上，休眠意味着坚硬的外壳与几乎停摆的代谢，而不是动物意义上的睡眠。

senses.title: Latency of a virus
senses.definition: the quiet phase in which a virus stays inside a cell without producing new particles or symptoms
senses.definitionCN: 病毒留在细胞内、不产生新颗粒也不引起症状的安静阶段
senses.example: Viral dormancy keeps the infection hidden for years.
senses.exampleCN: 病毒的潜伏让感染隐藏多年。
senses.why: Medicine borrowed the seed image: the agent is present but not growing, and can wake when conditions change.
senses.whyCN: 医学借用了种子的意象：病原在场却不生长，条件一变就可能醒来。

senses.title: A quiet stretch in a market or field
senses.definition: a figurative period in which an industry, market or project shows almost no activity but is not finished
senses.definitionCN: 行业、市场或项目几乎无活动、却并未终结的比喻性时期
senses.example: The dormancy of the housing market ended with a single cut in interest rates.
senses.exampleCN: 房地产市场的一段沉寂，因一次降息而结束。
senses.why: The metaphor drops the biology and keeps the shape: low activity, preserved capacity, later revival.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻舍弃生物学内容，只保留外形：低活动、保有能力、日后复苏。

senses.title: The depth of the resting state
senses.definition: the degree to which a resting organism resists waking, measured by how hard the block is to break
senses.definitionCN: 休眠中的生物抗拒苏醒的程度，以阻断有多难打破来衡量
senses.example: Biologists rate dormancy by the chilling hours needed to release it.
senses.exampleCN: 生物学家按解除休眠所需的低温小时数来划分休眠深度。
senses.why: Once dormancy can be measured, it acquires a scale, and the noun comes to name a point on that scale.
senses.whyCN: 一旦休眠可以被测量，它就有了刻度，这个名词也就用来指刻度上的某一点。

intro.en: Dormancy is an eighteenth-century English noun from dormant, which descends through French from Latin dormire 'to sleep'. The Latin verb is the source of a whole family of sleeping words.
intro.cn: dormancy 是十八世纪英语名词，来自 dormant，后者经法语源自拉丁 dormire「睡」。这个拉丁动词是一整族「睡眠」词的源头。

items.en: Dormire meant 'to sleep'. Its deeper origin is usually traced to a reconstructed Indo-European root for sleep, marked with an asterisk because it is rebuilt rather than recorded.
items.cn: dormire 意为「睡」。其更早来源一般追溯到原始印欧语中表示睡眠的重构词根；因是重建而非有记录，故带星号。

items.en: A dormitorium was a sleeping room. English dormitory descends from it, which is why the word for a hall of beds and the word for a sleeping seed look related.
items.cn: dormitorium 是「寝室」。英语 dormitory 由此而来，所以「宿舍」与「休眠的种子」看起来沾亲。

items.en: Old French used dormant, the present participle of dormir, for 'sleeping'. English borrowed the adjective in the thirteenth century.
items.cn: 古法语用 dormir 的现在分词 dormant 表示「睡着的」。英语在十三世纪借入这个形容词。

items.en: The abstract noun dormancy is recorded in the eighteenth century, formed with -cy on the model of other state nouns. The exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 抽象名词 dormancy 见于十八世纪，依照其他状态名词的模式加 -cy 构成。确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: Botany gave the word its modern precision by distinguishing true dormancy, which is internally controlled, from quiescence, which is forced by conditions.
items.cn: 植物学赋予这个词现代意义上的精确性：真正的休眠由内部控制，而静止状态由外部条件迫使。

items.en: Twentieth-century writing extended dormancy to viruses, markets and institutions, always keeping the promise of a later waking.
items.cn: 二十世纪的写作把 dormancy 扩展到病毒、市场与机构，始终保留「日后会醒来」的许诺。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same Latin sleeping root that are easily confused; group two holds rival terms for a life on hold.
note.cn: 第一组是同出拉丁「睡」词根、容易混淆的词；第二组是表示生命暂停的竞争性术语。

entries.definition: The adjective describing the state; dormancy is the noun, so one says seeds are dormant but seeds show dormancy.
entries.definitionCN: 描述该状态的形容词；dormancy 是名词，因此说种子处于休眠，而不说种子表现出休眠。

entries.definition: From Latin dormitorium 'sleeping room'; it names a place for sleeping, not a biological pause.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 dormitorium「寝室」，指睡觉的场所，不是生物性暂停。

entries.definition: From Old French dormeor 'sleeping room', applied to the roof window that lights such a room.
entries.definitionCN: 来自古法语 dormeor「寝室」，用来指给该房间采光的屋顶窗。

entries.definition: From Latin dormitio 'a sleeping', used in theology for a death described as falling asleep.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 dormitio「入睡」，神学中用来指被称为「睡着」的死亡。

entries.definition: A slowdown caused directly by external conditions, with no internal clock; the organism resumes the moment conditions improve.
entries.definitionCN: 由外部条件直接造成的放慢，没有内部时钟；条件一好就立刻恢复。

entries.definition: A deep seasonal dormancy of winter; dormancy is the wider category that contains it.
entries.definitionCN: 冬季的深度季节性休眠；dormancy 是包含它的更大类别。

entries.definition: The state of being present but not expressed, common for viruses and diseases; it stresses concealment rather than slowed growth.
entries.definitionCN: 存在却不表现的状态，常用于病毒与疾病；强调隐藏而非生长减慢。

entries.definition: A general halt in change or flow, from Greek stasis 'standing'; it need not imply a living thing that can wake.
entries.definitionCN: 变化或流动的总体停止，来自希腊 stasis「站立」；不必然暗示能醒来的活物。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Dormire is 'to sleep', so dormancy is the noun of sleep: a sleeping that a seed or spore can perform.
normal.cn: dormire 是「睡」，所以 dormancy 是「睡」的名词：种子或孢子也能进行的一种睡。

normal.en: The family runs dormant, dormancy, dormitory, dormer, dormition, dormitive.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 dormant、dormancy、dormitory、dormer、dormition、dormitive。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the biology: seed dormancy, break dormancy, deep dormancy, bud dormancy.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出生物学用法：种子休眠、打破休眠、深度休眠、芽休眠。

normal.en: Dormancy is internally controlled; quiescence is forced from outside, a distinction worth memorising as a pair.
normal.cn: 休眠由内部调控，静止由外部迫使；这对区别值得成对记住。

normal.en: The same root shows up in dormitory: a room for sleep, a seed for sleeping.
normal.cn: 同一词根出现在 dormitory：一间用来睡的房间，一粒用来睡的种子。

abstract.en: Picture a clock with its pendulum lifted and held, not removed.
abstract.cn: 想象一只钟的摆锤被抬起按住，而不是被拆掉。

abstract.en: Picture a letter sealed and put away, still readable when opened.
abstract.cn: 想象一封信被密封收起，打开时仍可读。

abstract.en: Picture a shop with the lights off but the stock still on the shelves.
abstract.cn: 想象一家关了灯的店，货架上的存货仍在。

examples.en: Deep dormancy keeps the seeds viable for years in dry soil.
examples.cn: 深度休眠使这些种子在干燥土壤中多年仍有活力。

examples.en: Seed dormancy spreads germination across several seasons instead of one week.
examples.cn: 种子休眠把萌发分散到几个季节，而不是挤在一周内。

examples.en: Viral dormancy keeps the infection hidden for years.
examples.cn: 病毒的潜伏让感染隐藏多年。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「多梦」——睡得多、梦得多，生长也停了 → 休眠

root: 拉丁 dormire「睡」+ 名词后缀 -ncy（经由 dormant 构成抽象状态名词）；dormire 更早一般追溯到原始印欧语表示睡眠的重构词根（星号形式为重构），确切音形存疑。英语 dormancy。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one gesture: life is put on hold without being ended. The gesture begins with seeds and buds, widens to spores and viruses, then to markets, and finally becomes a measurable depth.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个动作展开：把生命挂起，却不终结它。这个动作从种子与芽开始，扩到孢子与病毒，再到市场，最后成为一种可测量的深度。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a locked drawer holding a seed and a bud while the seasons turn outside.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只上锁的抽屉里放着种子与芽，抽屉外季节轮转。

branches.en: THE GENERAL PAUSE: life continues without growth, and the noun also measures how long the pause lasts.
branches.cn: 总体暂停：生命继续却不生长，名词还计量暂停持续多久。

branches.en: SEEDS AND BUDS: the coat or the chilling requirement decides when growth may restart.
branches.cn: 种子与芽：种皮或需冷量决定生长何时可以重启。

branches.en: SMALL AND HIDDEN: spores toughen and viruses go quiet, both present but not multiplying.
branches.cn: 微小而隐蔽：孢子变硬、病毒转静，都在场却不增殖。

branches.en: MARKET QUIET: an industry borrows the pause and waits for demand to return.
branches.cn: 市场沉寂：行业借用这个暂停，等待需求回来。

branches.en: MEASURED DEPTH: once the block can be timed, dormancy becomes a quantity.
branches.cn: 可测的深度：一旦阻断可以被计时，休眠就成为一个量。

intro.en: Dormancy is built on a Latin verb of sleeping; the same root reappears in rooms and windows, which makes the family unusually easy to read.
intro.cn: dormancy 建立在一个表示「睡」的拉丁动词上；同一词根还出现在房间与窗户里，使这个词族格外容易读。

latinIntro.en: Latin dormire 'to sleep' gives dormitorium 'sleeping room', dormitio 'a sleeping' and the adjective dormitivus; the English abstract noun adds -cy to dormant.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 dormire「睡」生出 dormitorium「寝室」、dormitio「入睡」与形容词 dormitivus；英语抽象名词则在 dormant 后加 -cy。

items.example: Dormire non potest.
items.exampleCN: 他睡不着。

items.example: The volcano is dormant but not extinct.
items.exampleCN: 这座火山休眠，但并未熄灭。

items.example: Dormancy protects the seed through winter.
items.exampleCN: 休眠保护种子度过冬天。

items.meaning: a building or room for sleeping
items.example: The students returned to the dormitory at ten.
items.exampleCN: 学生十点回到宿舍。

items.example: Light came through the dormer.
items.exampleCN: 光从屋顶天窗照进来。

items.meaning: a falling asleep; a death so described
items.meaningCN: 入睡；被称为安息的死亡
items.example: The feast commemorates her dormition.
items.exampleCN: 这个节庆纪念她的安息。

items.example: Old pharmacopoeias listed dormitive syrups.
items.exampleCN: 旧药典列有助眠糖浆。

items.meaning: a partial rest that can still be broken easily
items.example: Semi-dormancy lets the buds respond to a warm spell.
items.exampleCN: 半休眠让芽能对一段暖期作出反应。

items.example: The tubers lay dormantly under the soil.
items.exampleCN: 块茎以休眠状态躺在土下。

definition_zh: 生物地球化学循环（元素在生物、地质与化学过程共同驱动下，在空气、水、岩石与生物体之间循环的过程）
definition_en: the circulation of an element among air, water, rock and living organisms, driven jointly by biological, geological and chemical processes
core_image: 同一批原子在四个房间里轮转：空气、水、岩石、生命，每换一个房间就换一种化学身份，一本账记着进与出
scene: 课堂上老师把四个储库画成一个环路，让学生标出每一步的化学变化。 The biogeochemical cycle of sulphur links volcanic rock, seawater and living cells.
sceneCN: 这里 biogeochemical cycle 指「元素在生物、地质与化学共同驱动下的整个循环」（第 1 个义项：作为整体过程）；句意为硫的生物地球化学循环把火山岩、海水与活细胞连在一起。

pos.zh: 生物地球化学循环（术语短语，常带定冠词；复数直接加 -s 指不同元素或不同系统的循环）

senses.title: The loop as a whole
senses.titleCN: 作为整体的生物地球化学循环
senses.definition: the complete circuit of an element through air, water, rock and life
senses.definitionCN: 元素经空气、水、岩石与生命体走完一圈的完整回路
senses.example: The biogeochemical cycle of sulphur links volcanic rock, seawater and living cells.
senses.exampleCN: 硫的生物地球化学循环把火山岩、海水与活细胞连在一起。
senses.why: the phrase names a whole circuit in which biological, geological and chemical processes all take part.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语命名的是一个完整回路，生物、地质与化学过程全都参与其中。

senses.title: Reservoirs
senses.definition: the stores where an element sits, such as the atmosphere, ocean, soil or rock
senses.definitionCN: 元素停留的储存处，如大气、海洋、土壤或岩石
senses.example: The ocean is the largest reservoir in most biogeochemical cycles of carbon.
senses.exampleCN: 在多数碳的生物地球化学循环中，海洋是最大的储库。
senses.why: a cycle cannot be described until you say where the element waits.
senses.whyCN: 不先说清元素在哪里等待，就无法描述一个循环。

senses.title: Fluxes
senses.definition: the rates at which an element moves between reservoirs
senses.definitionCN: 元素在储库之间移动的速率
senses.example: Fluxes in the biogeochemical cycle are measured in tonnes per year.
senses.exampleCN: 生物地球化学循环中的通量以每年吨数计量。
senses.why: the loop is defined as much by its speeds as by its stores.
senses.whyCN: 循环既由储库定义，也由速度定义。

senses.title: The biological half
senses.definition: uptake, assimilation, growth, death and decomposition carried out by organisms
senses.definitionCN: 由生物完成的吸收、同化、生长、死亡与分解
senses.example: The biological half of the biogeochemical cycle runs on seasons.
senses.exampleCN: 生物地球化学循环中生物的那一半随季节运转。
senses.why: life accelerates the loop by pulling elements into tissue and releasing them again.
senses.whyCN: 生命通过把元素拉进组织再释放，加速了循环。

senses.title: The geological half
senses.definition: weathering, erosion, burial, sedimentation and tectonic uplift
senses.definitionCN: 风化、侵蚀、埋藏、沉积与构造抬升
senses.example: The geological half of the biogeochemical cycle sets its long rhythm.
senses.exampleCN: 地质那一半为生物地球化学循环定下漫长的节拍。
senses.why: rock stores and rock release give the loop its slow floor and ceiling.
senses.whyCN: 岩石的储存与释放给了循环缓慢的下限与上限。

senses.title: Chemical transformation
senses.definition: changes of oxidation state or bonding that decide whether an element can move or be used
senses.definitionCN: 决定元素能否移动或可用的氧化态与键合变化
senses.example: Chemical transformation decides whether iron stays in rock or dissolves.
senses.exampleCN: 化学形态转变决定铁留在岩石里还是溶解出来。
senses.why: the same atom behaves differently in each chemical form, so the loop is partly a sequence of reactions.
senses.whyCN: 同一个原子在不同化学形态下行为不同，因此循环部分是一串反应。

senses.title: Coupled cycles
senses.definition: the interlocking of element cycles so that a change in one alters the others
senses.definitionCN: 各元素循环彼此扣合，一处变化会改动其余
senses.example: Coupled biogeochemical cycles explain why adding nitrogen changes how carbon is stored.
senses.exampleCN: 耦合的生物地球化学循环解释了为何加入氮会改变碳的储存。
senses.why: elements do not cycle alone; the chemistry of one is the environment of another.
senses.whyCN: 元素不会各自循环；一种元素的化学环境就是另一种元素的处境。

senses.title: Timescales and feedback
senses.definition: the fast biological loops and slow geological loops whose mismatch produces feedback
senses.definitionCN: 快生物回路与慢地质回路之间的错配产生的反馈
senses.example: The mismatch of timescales inside the biogeochemical cycle is what makes it hard to model.
senses.exampleCN: 生物地球化学循环内部时间尺度的错配，正是它难以建模的原因。
senses.why: a process that takes days and one that takes epochs obey different rules, and their friction is the feedback.
senses.whyCN: 以天计的过程与以纪元计的过程遵守不同规则，它们的摩擦就是反馈。

senses.title: Human modification
senses.definition: the altered fluxes caused by burning, fertilising, mining, damming and land clearing
senses.definitionCN: 由燃烧、施肥、采矿、筑坝与开荒造成的通量改变
senses.example: Human activity has doubled several fluxes in the biogeochemical cycle of nitrogen.
senses.exampleCN: 人类活动使氮的生物地球化学循环中多条通量翻倍。
senses.why: once people move more material than nature does, the cycle must be described with human terms.
senses.whyCN: 一旦人搬运的物质超过自然，循环就必须用人类的词来描述。

intro.en: Biogeochemical cycle stacks Greek bios 'life', gē 'earth' and khēmeia 'metalworking', then adds kyklos 'wheel'. The phrase is a twentieth-century coinage of earth and life science, built once biogeochemistry became a recognised field in the 1920s.
intro.cn: biogeochemical cycle 叠起希腊 bios「生命」、gē「大地」与 khēmeia「冶炼」，再加上 kyklos「轮子」。这个短语是二十世纪地球与生命科学的造词，产生于生物地球化学在一九二〇年代成为公认领域之后。

items.en: Bios meant life and supplies the bio- of biology and biogeochemistry.
items.cn: bios 意为生命，提供 biology 与 biogeochemistry 的 bio-。

items.en: Gē meant earth and gives the geo- of geology, geography and geochemistry.
items.cn: gē 意为大地，给出 geology、geography 与 geochemistry 的 geo-。

items.en: Khēmeia named the art of working metals; through Arabic and Latin it became English chemistry.
items.cn: khēmeia 指冶炼金属之术；经阿拉伯语与拉丁语成为英语 chemistry。

items.en: Kyklos 'circle, wheel' passed through Latin cyclus into English cycle.
items.cn: kyklos「圆圈、轮子」经拉丁 cyclus 进入英语 cycle。

items.en: Vernadsky's biosphere work made the chemistry of life and rock a single subject, and the adjective followed.
items.cn: 维尔纳茨基的生物圈工作把生命与岩石的化学变成同一个课题，形容词随之出现。

items.en: Mid-century earth scientists applied cycle to these coupled element flows, fixing the phrase in textbooks.
items.cn: 二十世纪中期的地球科学家把 cycle 用于这些耦合的元素流动，使这个短语固定在教科书里。

note.en: Group one holds the shorter or narrower terms that are mistaken for this phrase; group two holds the named element cycles it includes.
note.cn: 第一组是最容易被当成这个短语的较短或较窄术语；第二组是它所包含的具体元素循环。

entries.definition: Describing something that involves life, rock and chemistry; alone it names no circuit.
entries.definitionCN: 描述同时涉及生命、岩石与化学的事物；单独使用并不命名任何回路。

entries.definition: A cycle of an element driven by rock and water alone; it leaves out the biological pump.
entries.definitionCN: 仅由岩石与水驱动的元素循环；它不含生物泵。

entries.definition: The recycling of nutrients within an ecosystem; it is a small, fast subset of the larger cycle.
entries.definitionCN: 生态系统内部的养分回收；它是更大循环中一个小而快的子集。

entries.definition: Any circulation of a chemical element; the term says nothing about how many processes drive it.
entries.definitionCN: 任何化学元素的循环；这个说法不说明由多少种过程驱动。

entries.definition: The circulation of carbon among air, sea, rock and life; it is the best-known biogeochemical cycle.
entries.definitionCN: 碳在空气、海洋、岩石与生命之间的循环；它是最著名的生物地球化学循环。

entries.definition: The circulation of nitrogen, notable for its huge atmospheric store and microbial steps.
entries.definitionCN: 氮的循环，以巨大的大气储库与微生物步骤著称。

entries.definition: A cycle dominated by rock stores rather than air, such as phosphorus; it is one kind of biogeochemical cycle.
entries.definitionCN: 由岩石储库而非空气主导的循环，如磷循环；它是生物地球化学循环的一种。

entries.definition: The planet's interacting air, water, rock and life; cycles run inside it but it is not a cycle.
entries.definitionCN: 行星互相作用的空气、水、岩石与生命；循环在其中运行，但它本身不是循环。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the four real roots plus the four real reservoirs of any element cycle.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：四个真实词根，加上任何元素循环的四个真实储库。

normal.en: bio is life, geo is earth, chemical is metalworking, cycle is a wheel: life and earth turning chemistry in a circle.
normal.cn: bio 是生命，geo 是大地，chemical 是冶炼，cycle 是轮子：生命与大地把化学转成一个圈。

normal.en: Four reservoirs: air, water, rock, life.
normal.cn: 四个储库：空气、水、岩石、生命。

normal.en: Two speeds: seasons for biology, epochs for geology.
normal.cn: 两种速度：生物按季节，地质按纪元。

normal.en: One accounting trick: store plus flux equals the whole story.
normal.cn: 一个核算诀窍：储库加通量就是全部故事。

normal.en: Vernadsky is the anchor name for the field behind the phrase.
normal.cn: 维尔纳茨基是这个短语背后学科的关键名字。

abstract.en: It is a relay race in which the baton is an atom and the runners are a forest, a river and a volcano.
abstract.cn: 它是一场接力赛，接力棒是一个原子，跑者是森林、河流与火山。

abstract.en: The cycle is a conversation between the fast and the slow.
abstract.cn: 这个循环是一场快与慢之间的对话。

abstract.en: Nothing is wasted; everything is only between appointments.
abstract.cn: 没有东西被浪费，一切只是处在两次约见之间。

examples.en: Each element has its own biogeochemical cycle, but the cycles interact.
examples.cn: 每种元素各有自己的生物地球化学循环，但各循环彼此作用。

examples.en: Ocean eddies influence the biogeochemical cycle of iron in the Southern Ocean.
examples.cn: 海洋涡旋影响南大洋中铁的生物地球化学循环。

examples.en: The course compares the biogeochemical cycle of carbon with that of phosphorus.
examples.cn: 这门课比较碳与磷的生物地球化学循环。

dict_mnemonic.text: bio（生命）+ geo（大地）+ chemical（化学）+ cycle（循环）＝生命与大地共同把元素转一圈；记四个储库与两种速度。

root: bio-（希腊 bios「生命」）+ geo-（希腊 gē「大地」）+ chemical（希腊 khēmeia「冶炼术」）+ cycle（希腊 kyklos「圆环」）；短语为二十世纪地球科学所立。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses move from the whole to its parts and uses: the circuit, reservoirs, fluxes, the biological half, the geological half, chemical form, coupling, timescale feedback and human change.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项从整体走向部件与用途：回路、储库、通量、生物那一半、地质那一半、化学形态、耦合、时间尺度反馈，以及人类改动。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one atom leaving air for a leaf, then soil, then a river, then a shell on the seabed, then rock, then a volcano, then air again.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个原子离开空气进入叶片，再到土壤、河流、海底贝壳、岩石、火山，最后回到空气。

branches.en: WHOLE AND RHYTHM: the circuit, then the mismatch of fast and slow loops that creates feedback.
branches.cn: 整体与节拍：先是回路，再是快慢回路错配造成的反馈。

branches.en: STATICS AND MOTION: reservoirs, then the fluxes between them.
branches.cn: 静与动：先是储库，再是储库之间的通量。

branches.en: TWO HALVES: the biological pump and the geological engine.
branches.cn: 两半：生物泵与地质引擎。

branches.en: CHEMICAL FORM: oxidation state and bonding deciding mobility.
branches.cn: 化学形态：氧化态与键合决定迁移能力。

branches.en: COUPLING AND HUMAN CHANGE: linked cycles, then the fluxes people have rewritten.
branches.cn: 耦合与人类改动：先是彼此扣合的循环，再是人改写过的通量。

intro.en: Biogeochemical cycle joins three Greek roots and an English adjective ending to a Greek noun for a wheel.
intro.cn: biogeochemical cycle 把三个希腊词根与一个英语形容词词尾，接在一个表示轮子的希腊名词上。

latinIntro.en: All four roots are Greek; Latin carried khēmeia through Arabic as alchimia and borrowed kyklos as cyclus, but has no native cognates for bios or gē.
latinIntro.cn: 四个词根都属希腊语；拉丁语把 khēmeia 经阿拉伯语作 alchimia 传入，并借入 kyklos 作 cyclus，但 bios 与 gē 在拉丁语中无本土同族词。

items.example: Bios opens the compound.
items.exampleCN: bios 开启了这个复合词。

items.example: Gē supplies the middle element.
items.exampleCN: gē 提供了中间那个成分。

items.example: Khēmeia became chemistry.
items.exampleCN: khēmeia 变成了 chemistry。

items.example: Chemistry supplies the third part.
items.exampleCN: chemistry 提供第三部分。

items.meaning: the study of life, rock and chemistry together
items.meaningCN: 合并研究生命、岩石与化学的学科
items.example: Biogeochemistry named the field in the 1920s.
items.exampleCN: 生物地球化学在一九二〇年代为这个领域命名。

items.example: Kyklos ends the phrase.
items.exampleCN: kyklos 收尾这个短语。

items.example: The cycle returns the element to its start.
items.exampleCN: 循环把元素送回起点。

items.example: Each reservoir has a capacity.
items.exampleCN: 每个储库都有容量。

items.example: Flux is measured per year.
items.exampleCN: 通量按年计量。

definition_zh: 水力发电的；利用水流能量发电的
definition_en: producing electricity from the energy of falling or flowing water
core_image: 高坝把河水蓄成平静的湖面，闸口放出的水柱冲向机房里的水轮机
scene: 峡谷里的高坝把河水拦成深湖，闸口放出的水柱冲进下游机房。 The valley relies on a hydroelectric dam for power.
sceneCN: 这里 hydroelectric 指「利用水流的能量发电的」（第 1 个义项：以落差水流驱动涡轮产生电力）；句意为这个峡谷依靠一座水电站大坝供电。图中可辨识物件：弧形坝体、闸门水柱、机房、下游河道。

pos.zh: 水力发电的（多作定语，也可作表语）

senses.title: Generating power from water
senses.definition: using falling or flowing water to drive turbines and produce electricity
senses.definitionCN: 利用落差水流或流动的水驱动涡轮并产生电力
senses.example: The valley relies on a hydroelectric dam for power.
senses.exampleCN: 这个峡谷依靠一座水电站大坝供电。
senses.why: hydro- supplies 'water' and electric supplies 'producing current', so the adjective says the current is made from water.
senses.whyCN: hydro- 提供「水」，electric 提供「产生电流」，因此这个形容词表示电流由水而来。

senses.title: Belonging to such a plant
senses.titleCN: 属于此类电站的（定语义）
senses.definition: describing a dam, station or turbine that belongs to a water-power system
senses.definitionCN: 描述属于水力发电系统的坝、站或涡轮机
senses.example: The hydroelectric station employs forty local workers.
senses.exampleCN: 这座水电站雇用了四十名当地工人。
senses.why: nouns like dam and station borrow the adjective to mark what kind of plant they are, so the word becomes a classifier.
senses.whyCN: dam、station 等名词借这个形容词标明电站种类，于是这个词成了分类标签。

senses.title: The electricity so produced
senses.titleCN: 这样发出的电（准名词义）
senses.definition: the current itself, when speakers shorten the noun phrase to the adjective
senses.definitionCN: 指电流本身，即说话人把名词短语省略后留下的形容词
senses.example: The grid buys hydroelectric from the mountain states.
senses.exampleCN: 电网从山区各州购买水电。
senses.why: English often lets an adjective stand for its noun, so hydroelectric can name the product as well as the process.
senses.whyCN: 英语常让形容词代替其名词，因此 hydroelectric 既可指过程，也可指产品。

senses.title: A branch of engineering and industry
senses.definition: the sector of design, construction and operation that builds water-power works
senses.definitionCN: 负责设计、建造与运营水力发电工程 的行业部门
senses.example: She trained as a hydroelectric engineer in the north.
senses.exampleCN: 她在北方接受水电站工程师的训练。
senses.why: a technique becomes a field when universities teach it and firms bid for its contracts.
senses.whyCN: 当大学开设课程、公司竞标合同，一种技术就变成一个领域。

senses.title: Hydraulic energy turned electric
senses.definition: the conversion of hydraulic energy into electrical energy in a machine
senses.definitionCN: 在机器中把水能转化为电能的过程
senses.example: The lab measured hydroelectric efficiency at ninety percent.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室测得水力发电效率为九成。
senses.why: physics uses the adjective for any process that changes hydraulic energy into electrical energy, whatever the scale.
senses.whyCN: 物理学用这个形容词指任何把水能变成电能的过程，不论规模。

senses.title: Low-carbon power in climate debate
senses.titleCN: 气候讨论中的低碳电力
senses.definition: power classed as low-carbon because no fuel is burned to make it
senses.definitionCN: 因发电不烧燃料而被归为低碳的电力
senses.example: The report counted hydroelectric as a clean resource.
senses.exampleCN: 报告把水电算作清洁资源。
senses.why: climate accounting groups technologies by emissions, and this label places water power among the clean ones.
senses.whyCN: 气候核算按排放给技术分组，这个标签把水电放进清洁一类。

senses.title: Converting an obvious natural fall
senses.titleCN: 抽象技术义：把现成落差转为可用形式
senses.definition: any system that converts a ready-made natural drop into a usable form of power
senses.definitionCN: 任何把现成的自然落差转化为可用动力的系统
senses.example: The engineers called the tide a hydroelectric opportunity.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师把潮汐称作一个水力发电式的机会。
senses.why: the word's shape only requires a gradient and a converter, so it stretches to tides and even to data flows.
senses.whyCN: 这个词的构造只要求一个落差和一个转换器，因此可延伸到潮汐甚至数据流。

senses.title: Big dams and their social cost
senses.titleCN: 大型水坝及其社会代价的象征义
senses.definition: a shorthand in public debate for large dams, including the villages they displace
senses.definitionCN: 公共讨论中对大型水坝的简称，也含被其淹没的村庄
senses.example: The word hydroelectric carried a promise and a protest.
senses.exampleCN: 水力发电这个词既带着承诺，也带着抗议。
senses.why: large dams flood valleys, so the adjective acquired a social charge that has nothing to do with volts.
senses.whyCN: 大型水坝会淹没河谷，因此这个形容词带上了一层与电压无关的社会情绪。

intro.en: Hydroelectric joins Greek hydro- 'water' with electric, a seventeenth-century adjective coined from Greek elektron 'amber'. The compound itself is a nineteenth-century technical formation. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: hydroelectric 把希腊语 hydro-「水」与 electric 组合起来；electric 是 17 世纪由希腊语 elektron「琥珀」造出的形容词。整个复合词是 19 世纪的技术造词。年代均为约数。

items.en: Hydōr was the Greek noun for water, with an irregular declension. Its Indo-European ancestry is reconstructed, not directly attested.
items.cn: hydōr 是希腊语中表示水的名词，变格不规则。其印欧语来源属于重构形式，并非直接实证。

items.en: The combining form hydro- entered scientific compounds such as hydraulics, hydrogen and hydrosphere.
items.cn: 组合形式 hydro- 进入 hydraulics、hydrogen、hydrosphere 等科学复合词。

items.en: Ēlektron meant 'amber'. Rubbing amber produces static charge, and that observed property gave the name to the whole phenomenon.
items.cn: ēlektron 意为「琥珀」。摩擦琥珀会产生静电，这一观察到的性质把名字给了整个现象。

items.en: In the seventeenth century electricus 'like amber' was coined for bodies that attract light objects, and English electric followed.
items.cn: 17 世纪造出 electricus「像琥珀的」，指能吸引轻小物体的物体，英语 electric 随后出现。

items.en: Hydroelectric appeared in the nineteenth century once turbines and generators made falling water a practical source of current.
items.cn: 当涡轮机与发电机使落水成为实用的电流来源，hydroelectric 在 19 世纪出现。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin and first date): the pre-Greek origin of elektron is unsettled, and no exact first citation for the compound is recorded.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源与首见年代）：elektron 在希腊语之前的来源无定论，这个复合词也没有确切的最早书证。

note.en: Group one holds words built on hydro- or on the electric stock that are easily confused; group two holds names for the same power under other labels.
note.cn: 第一组是同出 hydro- 或 electric 词干、容易混淆的词；第二组是同一动力的其他名称。

entries.definition: From Greek hydraulikos, built on hydōr plus aulos 'pipe': it means worked by water in a pipe or by liquid pressure, not by generating current.
entries.definitionCN: 来自希腊 hydraulikos，由 hydōr 加 aulos「管」构成：指由管中水或液体压力驱动，不指发电。

entries.definition: Hydro- plus Greek -genes 'born': the 'water-former', named because burning it makes water; it is an element, not a power system.
entries.definitionCN: hydro- 加希腊 -genes「生成」：意为「生成水者」，因燃烧它会产生水而得名；它是一种元素，不是动力系统。

entries.definition: The base adjective for anything driven by or producing current; hydroelectric adds the source of that current.
entries.definitionCN: 指由电流驱动或产生电流的基础形容词；hydroelectric 补充了电流的来源。

entries.definition: Built on electron plus -ic: it describes circuits that control signals, not power generated from water.
entries.definitionCN: 由 electron 加 -ic 构成：描述控制信号的电路，而非水力发出的电力。

entries.definition: The noun for the power itself; hydroelectric is the adjective describing the plant or the process.
entries.definitionCN: 指动力本身的名称；hydroelectric 是描述电站或过程的形容词。

entries.definition: The everyday phrase for power from water, including old mills; it is broader and less technical.
entries.definitionCN: 指水力的日常说法，也包括老磨坊；范围更宽，技术性较弱。

entries.definition: Power from the rise and fall of tides rather than from a river's fall; the machinery is similar but the source differs.
entries.definitionCN: 来自潮涨潮落的动力，而非河流落差；机械相似，来源不同。

entries.definition: The wider class that includes water, wind, solar and biomass; hydroelectric is one member.
entries.definitionCN: 更宽的类别，包含水能、风能、太阳能与生物质能；水电是其中一员。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: hydro- 'water' + electric 'current-making': the adjective spells out its own recipe.
normal.cn: hydro-「水」+ electric「产生电流的」：这个形容词把自己的配方写在了字面上。

normal.en: The family runs hydroelectric, hydroelectricity, hydropower, hydraulic, hydrogen.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 hydroelectric、hydroelectricity、hydropower、hydraulic、hydrogen。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the plant: hydroelectric dam, hydroelectric plant, hydroelectric station.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出电站：水电站大坝、水力发电厂、水电站。

normal.en: Greek ēlektron 'amber' explains why electricity is named after a stone that crackles when rubbed.
normal.cn: 希腊 ēlektron「琥珀」解释了为什么电以一个摩擦会响的石头命名。

normal.en: Hydro- also appears in hydraulics, where water works through pipes instead of turning a generator.
normal.cn: hydro- 也出现在 hydraulics 中，那里的水通过管道做功，而不去转动发电机。

abstract.en: Picture a waterfall that has been taught to sing in wires.
abstract.cn: 想象一道瀑布学会了在电线里歌唱。

abstract.en: Picture a lake held above the valley like a raised hand waiting to push.
abstract.cn: 想象一片湖被举在河谷上方，像一只抬起待推的手。

abstract.en: Picture a hill that keeps a battery charged simply by being tall.
abstract.cn: 想象一座山，仅凭自己够高就为电池充着电。

examples.en: The country built its first hydroelectric plant in the mountains.
examples.cn: 这个国家在山区建起了第一座水力发电厂。

examples.en: Hydroelectric output falls when the reservoirs run low.
examples.cn: 水库水位过低时，水力发电量会下降。

examples.en: The map marks every hydroelectric dam on the river.
examples.cn: 地图标出了这条河上的每一座水电站大坝。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「hydro（水）+ electric（电的）」——用水发出的电 → 水力发电的

root: 希腊 hydōr「水」（组合形式 hydro-）+ electric；electric 来自新拉丁 electricus「像琥珀的」，再上溯希腊 ēlektron「琥珀」。两个希腊成分拼成现代技术复合词。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one machine: water falls, a gate opens, a turbine spins, a generator turns, current leaves, and the same adjective then classifies plants, names the product, labels an industry and finally carries a social charge.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一台机器展开：水落下、闸门开启、涡轮旋转、发电机转动、电流送出，随后同一形容词用来分类电站、命名产品、标注行业，最后带上社会情绪。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a high dam holding a lake above a valley while water rushes through a gate into a machine hall.
core.cn: 核心意象：高坝把湖举在河谷上方，水流穿过闸门冲进机房。

branches.en: PHYSICAL CONVERSION: falling water drives a machine that changes hydraulic energy into current.
branches.cn: 物理转换：落水驱动机械，把水能变成电流。

branches.en: PLANT AND PRODUCT: the adjective classifies the dam and can also name the current it sells.
branches.cn: 电站与产品：形容词既分类大坝，也可指它所售的电流。

branches.en: INDUSTRY: engineering schools and construction firms turn the technique into a field.
branches.cn: 产业：工程院校与建设公司把这项技术变成一个领域。

branches.en: CLEAN AND GENERAL: climate accounting calls it clean, and the same shape stretches to any ready-made gradient.
branches.cn: 清洁与泛化：气候核算称其清洁，同一构造也延伸到任何现成落差。

branches.en: SOCIAL CHARGE: large dams flood valleys, so the word also stands for promise and protest.
branches.cn: 社会情绪：大型水坝淹没河谷，因此这个词也代表承诺与抗议。

intro.en: Hydroelectric is a modern compound of two Greek-derived elements. Each element is a combining form that still builds technical vocabulary, so the word can be read as 'water' plus 'current-making'.
intro.cn: hydroelectric 是两个希腊来源成分构成的现代复合词。每个成分都是仍在构成技术词汇的组合形式，因此这个词可读作「水」加「产生电流的」。

latinIntro.en: Latin electricus and electrum transmit the Greek amber word to English, while hydraulicus shows the same hydro- element in a different machine.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 electricus 与 electrum 把希腊的琥珀词传给英语，hydraulicus 则显示同一 hydro- 成分用在另一种机械上。

items.structure: Greek hydōr 'water' used as a combining form
items.example: Hydrology is the study of water on land.
items.exampleCN: 水文学研究陆地上的水。

items.example: The root names the driving substance.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根命名了驱动用的物质。

items.example: An electric motor turns the shaft.
items.exampleCN: 电动机转动轴。

items.example: The dam sells electricity to three provinces.
items.exampleCN: 这座坝向三个省售电。

items.meaning: a person who installs and repairs wiring
items.meaningCN: 安装与修理电线的人；电工
items.example: The electrician checked the switchboard.
items.exampleCN: 电工检查了配电盘。

items.meaning: worked by water or liquid pressure
items.example: The gate is raised by hydraulic rams.
items.exampleCN: 闸门由液压装置抬起。

items.example: Hydrogen burns to water vapour.
items.exampleCN: 氢燃烧后变成水蒸气。

items.example: Hydroelectricity supplied the winter load.
items.exampleCN: 水电供应了冬季负荷。

items.example: The valley relies on a hydroelectric dam for power.
items.exampleCN: 这个峡谷依靠一座水电站大坝供电。

latinEntries.meaning: like amber; producing attraction when rubbed
latinEntries.meaningCN: 像琥珀的；摩擦后产生吸引的

latinEntries.structure: electrum, electri (n., second declension; from Greek ēlektron)
hydraulicus, hydraulica, hydraulicum (adjective; from Greek hydraulikos)
latinEntries.meaning: of a water organ; worked by water

definition_zh: 珊瑚；珊瑚虫群体；珊瑚色；珊瑚制品
definition_en: a stony material built by tiny sea polyps, the animal colony itself, or the pink-orange colour of the precious kind
core_image: 海底一丛粉橙色的枝状硬骨，枝端还伸着细小的白色触手
scene: 浅海潜水时，向导指着一丛粉橙色的枝状硬骨，说明那些细小的触手是仍在取食的珊瑚虫。 The guide pointed to a branching pink-orange coral whose tiny polyps were still feeding.
sceneCN: 这里 coral 指「由珊瑚虫群体建造的活体珊瑚」（第 1 个义项：活着的珊瑚虫群体）；句意为向导指向一丛仍在取食的粉橙色枝状珊瑚。

pos.zh: 珊瑚；珊瑚虫群体
珊瑚（材料、制品）
珊瑚色的；珊瑚制的

derivatives.zh: 珊瑚的；珊瑚色的；珊瑚藻

senses.title: The living colony of polyps
senses.definition: a colony of small sea animals that build a shared skeleton around themselves
senses.definitionCN: 由许多细小海生动物构成的群体，它们在自己周围建造共同的骨骼
senses.example: The guide pointed to a branching coral whose polyps were still feeding.
senses.exampleCN: 向导指着一丛仍在取食的枝状珊瑚。
senses.why: Naturalists first took coral for a plant; once it was shown to be an animal, the same word came to name the living colony.
senses.whyCN: 博物学家最初把珊瑚当作植物；一旦证明它是动物，同一个词就开始指活的群体。

senses.title: The hard stony skeleton
senses.definition: the limy skeleton left by a coral colony, often branching or dome-shaped
senses.definitionCN: 珊瑚群体留下的钙质骨骼，常呈枝状或穹顶状
senses.example: The beach was made of broken coral and shell.
senses.exampleCN: 这片海滩由碎珊瑚和贝壳构成。
senses.why: The skeleton outlasts the animal, so the word transferred from the builder to the built thing.
senses.whyCN: 骨骼比动物活得久，于是这个词从建造者转到了被建造物上。

senses.title: The framework of a reef
senses.definition: coral as the main builder that raises a reef structure in shallow tropical seas
senses.definitionCN: 在浅热带海域抬升出礁体结构的主要造礁珊瑚
senses.example: Coral slowly raised a barrier along the edge of the island.
senses.exampleCN: 珊瑚沿海岛边缘慢慢筑起一道堡礁。
senses.why: In geology coral names the construction material of the reef, not the animal that made it.
senses.whyCN: 在地质语境里，coral 指礁体的建筑材料，而不是造它的动物。

senses.title: Polished coral as a material
senses.definition: the hard red or pink coral cut and polished for use in objects
senses.definitionCN: 被切割打磨、用于制作器物的红色或粉色硬珊瑚
senses.example: The workshop set a piece of coral into a silver ring.
senses.exampleCN: 工坊把一块珊瑚嵌进银戒指。
senses.why: Once cut and polished, the skeleton becomes a gem-like material, and the word follows the trade.
senses.whyCN: 一旦切割打磨，骨骼就成了类宝石的材料，词义也随行业走。

senses.title: The orange-pink colour
senses.definition: a soft orange-pink colour like precious red coral
senses.definitionCN: 像贵重红珊瑚那样的柔和橙粉色
senses.example: The walls were painted a warm coral.
senses.exampleCN: 墙面被刷成温暖的珊瑚色。
senses.why: The colour name is a straightforward transfer: the hue is named after the object that supplied the dye-like shade.
senses.whyCN: 颜色名是直接的转喻：这种色调以提供它的物件命名。

senses.title: Coral as ornament
senses.definition: beads, carvings or jewellery made from coral
senses.definitionCN: 用珊瑚制成的珠子、雕件或首饰
senses.example: A string of coral hung at her throat.
senses.exampleCN: 她颈间挂着一串珊瑚。
senses.why: The material is metonymy for the finished object, a common path from stuff to ornament.
senses.whyCN: 材料转指成品，这是从「材质」到「饰物」的常见路径。

senses.title: Fossil coral in rock
senses.definition: the remains of ancient coral preserved in limestone or shale
senses.definitionCN: 保存在石灰岩或页岩中的古代珊瑚遗骸
senses.example: Fossil coral in the cliff shows that this desert was once a sea.
senses.exampleCN: 崖壁里的珊瑚化石说明这片沙漠曾是海洋。
senses.why: Palaeontology keeps the name because the fossil keeps the shape, even though the animal is long gone.
senses.whyCN: 古生物学沿用这个名字，因为化石保留了形态，尽管动物早已消失。

senses.title: A protective talisman
senses.definition: red coral worn or hung as a charm against misfortune, especially for children
senses.definitionCN: 被佩戴或悬挂以避邪的红珊瑚，尤用于儿童
senses.example: The grandmother tied a small coral to the child's wrist.
senses.exampleCN: 祖母把一小块珊瑚系在孩子手腕上。
senses.why: Traditional belief gave the red material a protective power, so coral also names a charm rather than a substance.
senses.whyCN: 传统信仰赋予红色材料护佑之力，因此 coral 也指护身符，而不只是物质。

intro.en: Coral reached English through Old French from Latin, which had borrowed the word from Greek; the Greek source is not fully settled. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: coral 经古法语、拉丁语进入英语，拉丁语又是从希腊语借来的；希腊语的来源尚无定论。年代均为约数。

items.en: Korallion was the name of the red coral of the Mediterranean. Its deeper origin is not established; a Semitic loan is a common hypothesis, not a proven fact.
items.cn: korallion 是地中海红珊瑚的名称。其更深来源没有定论；源自闪米特语是一种常见假说，并非已证事实。

items.en: Latin took the Greek word as corallium and used it for the red skeletal material, which Romans carved into beads and charms.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入为 corallium，指红色的骨骼材料，罗马人把它雕成珠子和护符。

items.en: Old French coral carried the word into English in the twelfth century, at first for the precious red material rather than for a living animal.
items.cn: 古法语 coral 在 12 世纪把这个词带入英语，最初指贵重的红色材料，而非活体动物。

items.en: For centuries coral was classed as a sea plant; eighteenth-century naturalists showed that the polyps are animals, and the zoological sense followed.
items.cn: 数百年来珊瑚被归为海生植物；18 世纪的博物学家证明珊瑚虫是动物，动物学义随之出现。

items.en: The colour name coral, for the soft orange-pink of the precious material, became common in English dress and decoration writing.
items.cn: 指贵重材料那种柔和橙粉色的颜色名 coral，在英语服饰与装饰文字中逐渐通行。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper root): the Greek korallion has no agreed etymology, and the Semitic Origin hypothesis is one proposal among several, so no single source is asserted here.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词根）：希腊 korallion 没有公认的词源，闪米特语来源只是若干假说之一，此处不武断选定一种。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same coral stock that are easily interchanged; group two holds reef and shell words with neighbouring meanings.
note.cn: 第一组是同出 coral 词族、容易互换的词；第二组是意义相邻的礁与壳类词。

entries.definition: The plural counts colonies or kinds; coral as a mass material stays singular.
entries.definitionCN: 复数形式计数群体或种类；作物质材料时仍用单数 coral。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning of or like coral; as a noun it also names red coralline algae, a different organism.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，意为珊瑚的或似珊瑚的；作名词时还指珊瑚藻，那是另一种生物。

entries.definition: Built with -oid 'like', so it describes a branching shape without claiming the material is coral.
entries.definitionCN: 由 -oid「像」构成，描述枝状形态，并不表示材料真是珊瑚。

entries.definition: A reef is the whole wave-resistant structure; coral is one builder within it, alongside algae and other organisms.
entries.definitionCN: 礁指整座抗浪结构；珊瑚只是其中的建造者之一，还有藻类及其他生物参与。

entries.definition: One coral animal is a polyp; coral names the colony and its skeleton, not the individual.
entries.definitionCN: 单个珊瑚动物叫 polyp；coral 指群体及其骨骼，而非单个个体。

entries.definition: A ridge of rock, sand or coral near the surface; it may be built by coral but need not be.
entries.definitionCN: 靠近水面的一道岩石、沙或珊瑚脊；它可以由珊瑚建造，但并非必然。

entries.definition: The hard outer case of a mollusc or other animal; coral is an internal skeleton built by a colony, not a shell.
entries.definitionCN: 软体动物等的外壳；珊瑚是群体建造的骨骼，不是外壳。

entries.definition: A rock made largely of calcium carbonate, often from coral and shell debris; it is the stone, not the animal.
entries.definitionCN: 主要由碳酸钙构成的岩石，常来自珊瑚与贝壳碎屑；它指岩石，不指动物。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Coral names both the animal colony and the stone it leaves behind, so context decides which is meant.
normal.cn: coral 既指活体群体，也指它留下的石头，靠上下文判断指哪一个。

normal.en: The colour coral is simply the colour of red coral, not a separate root.
normal.cn: 颜色义 coral 就是红珊瑚的颜色，并非另一个词根。

normal.en: Coral reef and coral island are fixed compounds; reef alone can be rock or sand.
normal.cn: coral reef 与 coral island 是固定复合词；单说 reef 则可能是岩礁或沙洲。

normal.en: Coralline and coralloid both start with coral but point to 'of coral' and 'like coral' respectively.
normal.cn: coralline 与 coralloid 都以 coral 开头，但分别指「珊瑚的」与「像珊瑚的」。

normal.en: Coral bleaching is the fixed phrase for the whitening that follows the loss of algal partners.
normal.cn: 珊瑚失去共生藻后变白，固定说法是 coral bleaching。

abstract.en: Picture a city built by animals that never leave home, each adding a room of stone.
abstract.cn: 想象一座由从不离家的动物建起的城市，每只都添一间石屋。

abstract.en: Picture a pink branch that is soft while alive and becomes jewellery when dead.
abstract.cn: 想象一根粉色的枝，活着时柔软，死后变成首饰。

abstract.en: Picture a desert cliff holding the shape of a sea that vanished.
abstract.cn: 想象一面沙漠崖壁里留着早已消失的海洋的形状。

examples.en: Coral grows only where the water stays warm and clear.
examples.cn: 珊瑚只在水温温暖、水质清澈的地方生长。

examples.en: The island is a ring of coral around a drowned crater.
examples.cn: 这座岛是一圈环绕着沉没火山口的珊瑚。

examples.en: She chose a coral dress for the summer wedding.
examples.cn: 她为夏季婚礼选了一条珊瑚色的裙子。

dict_mnemonic.text: coral 读起来像「口若」——珊瑚枝一条条张开小口，像在不停地开口吃东西

root: 希腊 korallion「红珊瑚」→ 拉丁 corallium → 古法语 coral；korallion 的更深来源不确定，闪米特语来源只是一种假说。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one object from life to stone to symbol: the living colony, its skeleton, the reef it raises, the polished material, the colour, the ornament, the fossil, and the charm.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项让同一物件从生命走到石头再走到象征：活体群体、骨骼、抬升的礁、打磨的材料、颜色、饰品、化石与护符。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: pink branching stone with tiny white tentacles at the tips.
core.cn: 核心意象：粉色的枝状石头，枝端伸出细小的白色触手。

branches.en: BUILDER AND BUILT: the colony makes the stone, then the stone outlasts the colony.
branches.cn: 建造者与被建造物：群体造出石头，石头又比群体活得久。

branches.en: CONSTRUCTION: in geology the material is the reef itself.
branches.cn: 建筑：在地质语境中，这种材料就是礁体。

branches.en: MATERIAL TO ORNAMENT: cutting and polishing turn skeleton into gem and then into jewellery.
branches.cn: 从材料到饰品：切割打磨把骨骼变成宝石，再变成首饰。

branches.en: COLOUR BY METONYMY: the hue is named directly after the precious red kind.
branches.cn: 转喻得色：色调直接以贵重的红珊瑚命名。

branches.en: FROM STONE TO SYMBOL: the fossil proves an ancient sea, the charm promises protection.
branches.cn: 从石到象征：化石证明古海，护符许诺护佑。

intro.en: Coral is a borrowed noun with no productive English prefix; its family is built by compounding and by the suffixes -ine and -oid.
intro.cn: coral 是借入名词，没有能产的英语前缀；其词族靠复合与后缀 -ine、-oid 构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin corallium and Greek korallion are the source forms; corallum is the Latin noun used in natural history for a coral colony.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 corallium 与希腊 korallion 是来源形式；corallum 是博物学中用于指珊瑚群体的拉丁名词。

items.meaning: red coral, and later any coral
items.meaningCN: 红珊瑚；后泛指各类珊瑚
items.example: Coral was once classed as a plant.
items.exampleCN: 珊瑚曾被归为植物。

items.example: The reef holds hundreds of corals.
items.exampleCN: 这座礁有数百种珊瑚。

items.example: Coralline means belonging to coral.
items.exampleCN: coralline 意为属于珊瑚的。

items.meaning: of coral; also a red coralline alga
items.example: Coralline algae cement the reef frame.
items.exampleCN: 珊瑚藻把礁体胶结起来。

items.example: The suffix marks resemblance, not identity.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀标记相似，而非同一。

items.example: The mineral forms coralloid branches.
items.exampleCN: 这种矿物形成珊瑚状的枝。

items.meaning: a reef built chiefly by coral
items.example: The coral reef shelters the lagoon.
items.exampleCN: 珊瑚礁护住了潟湖。

items.meaning: an island made largely of coral
items.example: Coral islands rise only a few metres above the sea.
items.exampleCN: 珊瑚岛只高出海面几米。

items.example: The corallum is the whole skeletal frame.
items.exampleCN: corallum 指整个骨骼框架。

definition_zh: n. 拱门通道；拱形门洞（可通行的拱下空间）
definition_en: A passage roofed by an arch, or the arched opening itself, so that people can walk through under the curve.
core_image: 头顶弯成一道拱，底下留出一条能走人的路
scene: 穿过那道拱门就是老城的集市。 Beyond the archway lies the old town market.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：archway 指拱下可以通行的那条通道，重点在「能走过去」。

pos.zh: 拱门通道；拱形门洞

senses.title: A passage under an arch
senses.definition: a walkable space roofed by an arch, connecting one area to another
senses.definitionCN: 以拱为顶、可通行的空间，把一处与另一处连起来
senses.example: We stepped through the archway into a quiet courtyard.
senses.exampleCN: 我们穿过拱道，走进一个安静的院子。
senses.why: The word is arch plus way, so it names not the curve alone but the road that the curve makes possible.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是 arch 加 way，所以它指的不只是那道弯，而是那道弯让出来的路。

senses.title: The arched opening as a structure
senses.definition: the arched entrance considered as a built feature, whether or not anyone passes through it
senses.definitionCN: 被当作建筑构件看待的拱形入口，不论是否有人从中通行
senses.example: The archway was carved with vines and birds.
senses.exampleCN: 拱门上雕着藤蔓与鸟。
senses.why: Here attention shifts from walking to building: the same opening is described as masonry rather than as a route.
senses.whyCN: 这里注意力从「走」转到「建」：同一个洞口被当作砌体而非路线来描述。

intro.en: Archway is arch plus way. Arch comes from Latin arcus, a bow, through Old French arche; way is native Old English weg. The compound is recorded in the eighteenth century.
intro.cn: archway 是 arch 加 way。arch 来自拉丁语 arcus「弓」，经古法语 arche；way 是古英语本族词 weg。这个复合词记录于 18 世纪。

items.en: Latin arcus meant a bow, and then any curved structure spanning a gap.
items.cn: 拉丁语 arcus 意为「弓」，进而指任何跨越缺口的弧形结构。

items.en: Old French arche named the curved span, the form that gave English arch.
items.cn: 古法语 arche 指弧形跨度，这个形式给出了英语 arch。

items.en: Middle English arche was used for bridges, doorways and the brows of a face alike.
items.cn: 中古英语 arche 同样用于桥、门洞与眉毛。

items.en: Way is native, from Old English weg, a road or course, cousin to German Weg.
items.cn: way 是本族词，来自古英语 weg「路、行程」，与德语 Weg 同源。

items.en: English joined the two in the eighteenth century to name a passage roofed by an arch.
items.cn: 英语在 18 世纪把两者合成，指以拱为顶的通道。

items.en: Today archway is the ordinary word for an arched entrance in gardens, campuses and old towns.
items.cn: 如今 archway 是园林、校园与老城中拱形入口的常用词。

note.en: The look-alike group separates arch, the curve alone, from archway, the passage under it; the near-meaning group lists other words for a way in.
note.cn: 形近组把只指弧形的 arch 与指拱下通道的 archway 分开；近义组列出其他表示入口的词。

entries.definition: A curved span over an opening.
entries.definitionCN: 洞口上方的弧形跨度。

entries.definition: A row of arches along a walk.
entries.definitionCN: 沿通道排列的一排拱。

entries.definition: Someone who shoots with a bow.
entries.definitionCN: 用弓射箭的人。

entries.definition: A main public road.
entries.definitionCN: 主要公路。

entries.definition: An opening that gives entry.
