definition_zh: 朝贡体系；以进贡、册封与回赐串成的区域秩序；（引申）以让利换取顺从的安排
definition_en: a regional order in which lesser states present goods and envoys to a dominant power and receive titles and gifts in return
core_image: 使团抬着本地物产沿驿道进京，礼部逐项核对贡单，回赐的绢帛与印玺随后装箱南归
scene: 驿道尽头，使团把本地的马匹与香料抬上台阶，礼部官员逐项核对贡单，回赐的绢帛与印玺随后装箱南归。 The tribute system turned a flow of horses and spices into an ordered queue at the capital gate.
sceneCN: 这里「朝贡体系」指以进贡、册封与回赐串成的区域秩序（第 1 个义项：作为制度整体）；句意为朝贡体系把马匹与香料的流动排成京城门前的一条有序队列。

pos.zh: 朝贡体系；朝贡制度（可数，指一套安排；亦作不可数，指该秩序整体）

derivatives.zh: 贡品；致敬之词（拉丁 tributum「所分配之物」转指所纳之物，由缴纳转指所献之物）
支流的；纳贡的 / 藩属国（拉丁 tributarius「纳税的」，由纳贡者转指汇入干流的支流）
藩属国（tributary + state，由纳贡关系转指政治地位）

senses.title: The system as a whole
senses.definition: the whole set of rules, rituals and exchanges that link a dominant power with lesser states
senses.definitionCN: 把主导国与较小国家联结起来的那一整套规则、礼仪与往来
senses.example: Historians treat the tribute system as a single framework rather than a list of separate deals.
senses.exampleCN: 史学家把朝贡体系当作一个整体框架，而不是一桩桩彼此独立的交易。
senses.why: system names an organized whole, so the phrase points to the arrangement rather than to any one payment.
senses.whyCN: system 指一个有组织的整体，因此这个词组指向整套安排，而非某一笔缴纳。

senses.title: Paying tribute
senses.definition: the act of presenting goods and envoys to a superior power at fixed intervals
senses.definitionCN: 按固定周期向地位更高的政权呈上货物与使节的行为
senses.example: Paying tribute bought peace more cheaply than garrisoning the frontier.
senses.exampleCN: 与其在边境驻军，进贡换和平更省钱。
senses.why: tribute began as the name of a payment, so the phrase can name the recurring act rather than the whole order.
senses.whyCN: tribute 本是一笔缴纳的名称，因此这个词组也可指反复进行的缴纳行为。

senses.title: The goods delivered
senses.definition: the specific goods carried inward, such as silk, horses, spices or rare metals
senses.definitionCN: 运入的具体货物，如丝绸、马匹、香料或稀有金属
senses.example: The ledger lists tribute from the south as ivory, ebony and live birds.
senses.exampleCN: 账册把南方所纳的贡品记为象牙、乌木与活鸟。
senses.why: the concrete reading is the oldest one: tribute is first a thing handed over before it is a policy.
senses.whyCN: 具体义最古老：贡首先是交出去的东西，然后才成其为一项制度。

senses.title: Ritual submission
senses.definition: the ceremonial acknowledgment of a superior rank, performed through kneeling, titles and dated embassies
senses.definitionCN: 通过跪拜、称号与定期使团对更高地位的仪式性承认
senses.example: Ritual submission mattered more than the market value of the gifts.
senses.exampleCN: 礼仪上的臣服比礼物市价更重要。
senses.why: the order ran on recognition rather than force, so the ceremony itself counted as the substance.
senses.whyCN: 这套秩序靠承认而非武力运转，仪式本身就是实质。

senses.title: Trade inside ritual
senses.definition: commerce carried on under ceremonial forms, with gifts functioning as exchanged goods
senses.definitionCN: 在礼仪形式下进行的商业往来，礼物实际充当交换的商品
senses.example: Much of the trade inside ritual never looked like trade at all.
senses.exampleCN: 以礼为壳的贸易，大半看上去根本不像贸易。
senses.why: since both sides wanted goods, the ritual frame became the accepted channel for exchange.
senses.whyCN: 双方都要货物，礼仪框架便成了被接受的交换渠道。

senses.title: Investiture and return gifts
senses.definition: the titles, seals and goods sent back, which confirmed a ruler's place in the hierarchy
senses.definitionCN: 回送的名号、印玺与货物，确认某位统治者在等级中的位置
senses.example: Investiture and return gifts made the hierarchy visible to every neighbour.
senses.exampleCN: 册封与回赐让周边所有邻邦都看得见这套等级。
senses.why: the return leg completed the circuit: a gift back was a receipt of rank.
senses.whyCN: 回程那一段闭合了循环：回赐就是对名分的收据。

senses.title: Costly appeasement, by analogy
senses.titleCN: 引申：以让利换顺从的安排
senses.definition: any arrangement in which a weaker party buys tolerance by handing over value
senses.definitionCN: 较弱一方靠交出利益来换取容忍的任何安排
senses.example: Critics called the subsidy a modern tribute system in plain clothes.
senses.exampleCN: 批评者把这项补贴称作换了装的现代朝贡体系。
senses.why: the analogy keeps the shape of the old order and drops its rituals, leaving only payment for tolerance.
senses.whyCN: 这一类比保留了旧秩序的形状而剥掉礼仪，只剩为容忍而付费。

senses.title: A model in the archive
senses.titleCN: 作为史学分析框架的概念
senses.definition: an analytic model used by historians to describe a regional order, not a term the participants used
senses.definitionCN: 史学家用来描述某种区域秩序的分析模型，而非当时人自称的说法
senses.example: The model in the archive has been revised to include private sea trade.
senses.exampleCN: 这一分析框架已被修订，以纳入民间海上贸易。
senses.why: the label was coined by later scholars, so it works as a lens that can be tested and rewritten.
senses.whyCN: 这个标签由后来的学者造出，因此它是一面可被检验、也可被改写的透镜。

intro.en: Tribute goes back to Latin tributum 'that which is paid', from tribuere 'to allot, assign'; system comes from Greek systema 'an organized whole'. The compound is a modern scholarly label. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: tribute 上溯拉丁 tributum「所缴纳之物」，来自 tribuere「分配、拨给」；system 来自希腊 systema「有组织的整体」。整个词组是近代学术标签。年代均为约数。

items.en: Tribuere meant 'to allot, assign, grant', and tributum was what was assigned or paid over. The money sense is older than the political one.
items.cn: tribuere 意为「分配、拨给、给予」，tributum 即被分配或缴出之物。钱财义比政治义更早。

items.en: Tribuere came from tribus, a division of the Roman people. The deeper origin of tribus is not established; the old explanation that it meant 'a third part' is a hypothesis, not a demonstrated derivation.
items.cn: tribuere 来自 tribus，即罗马民众的划分单位。tribus 的更深来源未得到证明；旧说认为它本指「三分之一」，那只是假说，并非已证实的派生。

items.en: Systema meant 'an organized whole', built from syn- 'together' and histanai 'to set up, stand'. It passed into Latin and then into English as system.
items.cn: systema 意为「有组织的整体」，由 syn-「共同」与 histanai「设立、站立」构成，经拉丁语进入英语为 system。

items.en: The fixed phrase tribute system was taken up in twentieth-century English writing on East Asian diplomacy, where it named a whole order rather than a single payment.
items.cn: tribute system 这一固定说法在 20 世纪论东亚外交的英语著述中被采用，用来指整套秩序而非单笔缴纳。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date and scope): no exact first citation is recorded, the phrase is a later analytic label rather than a self-description, and the pre-Latin origin of tribus remains a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代与适用范围）：没有确切的最早书证；这一说法是后出的分析标签，而非当时人的自称；tribus 在拉丁语之前的来源仍属重构形式。

note.en: Group one gathers words from the same Latin verb and the same Greek noun; group two gathers near neighbours with overlapping political meaning.
note.cn: 第一组是同出拉丁动词与希腊名词的词；第二组是政治含义彼此交叠的近义词。

entries.definition: An adjective or noun for a state that pays tribute or a river that feeds a larger one; it names one member, not the whole framework.
entries.definitionCN: 指纳贡之国或汇入干流的支流，形容词或名词；它指其中一个成员，而非整套框架。

entries.definition: The single payment or the praise offered to a person; the compound adds system and so widens the scope to an order.
entries.definitionCN: 指单笔缴纳，或对某人的敬意之词；加上 system 后范围扩大为一套秩序。

entries.definition: Ad- 'to' plus tribuere: to assign a quality or cause to someone, so it shares the root but not the payment sense.
entries.definitionCN: ad-「向」加 tribuere：把某种性质或原因归于某人，词根相同而无缴纳之义。

entries.definition: Dis- 'apart' plus tribuere: to allot in pieces to many recipients, which keeps the original sense of assigning.
entries.definitionCN: dis-「分开」加 tribuere：把份额分给许多人，保留了「分配」的原义。

entries.definition: The relation in which one state controls another's foreign affairs while the lesser one keeps internal rule; it is the legal frame the tribute system dressed in ritual.
entries.definitionCN: 一国控制另一国外交、后者保留内部治理的关系；它是朝贡体系以礼仪包装的那套法理框架。

entries.definition: Leadership by one state through power and consent rather than ceremony; it stresses influence, not gifts and titles.
entries.definitionCN: 一国凭实力与默认取得的领导地位，不靠仪式；强调影响力，而非礼物与封号。

entries.definition: A state bound to a stronger one by oath and military obligation, a European feudal notion that only partly fits the tribute model.
entries.definitionCN: 以效忠誓言与军事义务从属强国之国，属欧洲封建概念，只部分对应朝贡模式。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: tribuere 'to allot': tribute is what was allotted and then handed over.
normal.cn: tribuere「分配」：tribute 就是被分配、再交出去的那一份。

normal.en: The family runs tribute, tributary, attribute and distribute, all from the same Latin verb.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 tribute、tributary、attribute、distribute，全出同一个拉丁动词。

normal.en: system is syn- 'together' plus histanai 'set up': a whole standing together.
normal.cn: system 是 syn-「共同」加 histanai「设立」：各部分共同立起来的一个整体。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the frame: pay tribute, send a tribute mission, a tributary state.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出这套框架：进贡、派遣朝贡使团、藩属国。

normal.en: Chinese names the same order by a phrase meaning presenting at court, which keeps the ceremony in view.
normal.cn: 同一秩序的中文说法是「朝贡」，即到朝廷献物，始终带着仪式的画面。

abstract.en: Picture a long corridor where every gift must pass through a gate before it counts as anything.
abstract.cn: 想象一条长廊，任何礼物都要先过一道门，才算数。

abstract.en: Picture two rulers exchanging boxes that contain the same goods in opposite directions.
abstract.cn: 想象两位君主互送箱子，箱中货物朝相反方向流动。

abstract.en: Picture a map drawn not with borders but with arrows pointing inward.
abstract.cn: 想象一张地图不画边界，只画一支支向内的箭头。

examples.en: The tribute system kept the frontier quiet for two centuries.
examples.cn: 朝贡体系让边境安定了两个世纪。

examples.en: Envoys were graded by the size of their tribute.
examples.cn: 使节的等级按所纳贡品的多寡排定。

examples.en: Modern aid programmes are sometimes read as a tribute system in reverse.
examples.cn: 现代援助计划有时被读作反向的朝贡体系。

dict_mnemonic.text: tribute（进贡）+ system（体系）＝ 一圈向内送礼、再向外回礼的秩序；记「货往里走，名往外发」。

root: tribute：拉丁 tributum「所缴纳之物」，来自 tribuere「分配、拨给」，再上溯 tribus「民众的划分」，其更深来源不确定；system：希腊 systema「有组织的整体」= syn-「共同」+ histanai「设立」。整个词组为近代学术标签。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one circuit: goods travel inward, rank is acknowledged, titles and gifts travel back, and the whole circuit is finally read as a model that later scholars can revise.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一条回路展开：货物向内，名分被承认，封号与礼物向外，最后整条回路被读成一个可供后人修订的模型。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a gate where goods enter and sealed titles leave, and everyone reads the queue as rank.
core.cn: 核心意象：一道门，货物进去、印玺出来，所有人都把这条队列读成等级。

branches.en: THE CIRCUIT AND ONE PAYMENT: the whole arrangement, then the single act that keeps it running.
branches.cn: 整条回路与单笔缴纳：先看整套安排，再看维持它运转的那一次行为。

branches.en: WHAT MOVES: the concrete goods that make the circuit visible.
branches.cn: 什么在流动：让整条回路看得见的具体货物。

branches.en: TWO HALVES OF RECOGNITION: the bow inward and the seal outward are one exchange of rank.
branches.cn: 承认的两半：向内的跪拜与向外的印玺，是同一次名分的交换。

branches.en: THE HIDDEN MARKET: ceremony becomes the accepted channel for trade.
branches.cn: 藏在礼下的市场：仪式成为贸易被接受的通道。

branches.en: FROM PRACTICE TO LENS: first a modern analogy, then an analytic model open to revision.
branches.cn: 从做法到透镜：先是现代类比，再是可被修订的分析模型。

intro.en: The phrase joins a Latin noun built on a verb of allotting with a Greek noun meaning an organized whole, so both halves can be read morpheme by morpheme.
intro.cn: 这个词组把拉丁语中由「分配」动词构成的名词，与希腊语中意为「有组织整体」的名词接在一起，两半都可按语素读出。

latinIntro.en: Latin tribuere gives tribute, tributary, attribute and distribute; Greek syn- plus histanai gives system, systematic and systemic.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 tribuere 衍生 tribute、tributary、attribute、distribute；希腊 syn- 加 histanai 衍生 system、systematic、systemic。

items.example: The verb supplies both the gift and the act of giving it.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词同时给出礼物与送礼的动作。

items.structure: tribuere + -tum (past participle used as a noun)
items.example: Tributum first named a levy, then a gift to a superior.
items.exampleCN: tributum 先指征收之物，后指献给上位者的礼物。

items.example: A tributary stream feeds the main river.
items.exampleCN: 支流汇入干流。

items.meaning: to assign as a quality or cause
items.example: They attribute the delay to the weather.
items.exampleCN: 他们把延误归因于天气。

items.example: Volunteers distribute the supplies.
items.exampleCN: 志愿者分发物资。

items.example: The tax system has three tiers.
items.exampleCN: 税制有三个层级。

items.example: They made a systematic survey of the coast.
items.exampleCN: 他们对海岸做了系统调查。

items.meaning: affecting the whole rather than a part
items.example: The failure was systemic, not local.
items.exampleCN: 这次失灵是整体性的，而非局部的。

latinEntries.structure: systema, systematis (n., third declension, from Greek)

definition_zh: 歧义；含糊；模棱两可；犹豫不决；（意图的）不确定
definition_en: the quality of having more than one possible meaning, of being unclear, or of a state of doubt in which the mind cannot settle
core_image: 一句话被同时驱向两条路：两种读法都站得住，谁也没被甩开
scene: 审稿人读到「他们给旧船刷了漆和发动机」这一句，先笑出声，随后在页边写下批注。 The reviewer reads the sentence 'they painted the old boat and the engine', laughs, and notes the structural ambiguity in the margin.
sceneCN: 这里 ambiguity 是「句法歧义」（第 4 个义项：句子结构可作两种切分）；句意：审稿人读到这句话先笑出声，随后在页边记下它的句法歧义。场景要点：稿纸页边的批注、被圈出的 and、两种颜色的修改笔、停住的笔尖。

pos.zh: 歧义；含糊；模棱两可；犹豫不决

collocations.zh: 道德上的含混（人物或结局难以简单评判）

derivatives.zh: 有歧义的；含糊不清的；模棱两可的

senses.title: Doubting, unable to decide
senses.titleCN: 犹疑不决：心智停不下来
senses.definition: the state of being unable to decide or of hesitating between possibilities
senses.definitionCN: 无法作出决定、在几种可能之间犹豫不定的状态
senses.example: His ambiguity about the job offer showed in the way he kept changing the subject.
senses.exampleCN: 他对这份工作邀请的犹豫，表现在他总把话题岔开。
senses.why: This is the earliest English sense, recorded c.1400. Latin ambigere meant 'to be driven around', so the mind here is not empty of meaning; it is pulled first one way and then the other.
senses.whyCN: 这是英语最早的义项，约记录于 1400 年。拉丁语 ambigere 意为“被驱赶着转来转去”，所以这里并非“没有意思”，而是心智先被拉向一边、又被拉向另一边。

senses.title: Two meanings in one word
senses.titleCN: 一词两义：同一个词被读出两种意思
senses.definition: the quality of a word or phrase that can be understood in two or more different ways
senses.definitionCN: 一个词或短语可以被理解成两种或多种不同意思的性质
senses.example: The ambiguity of 'bank' made the joke work.
senses.exampleCN: bank 一词的歧义让这个笑话成立了。
senses.why: Once ambiguity names the word rather than the mind, the two directions of ambigere become two readings of one form. The word itself is the crossroads where both roads stay open.
senses.whyCN: 当 ambiguity 指的不是心智而是词语时，ambigere 的两个方向就变成同一个词形的两种读法。词本身就是那个两条路都敞开的十字路口。

senses.title: The meaning is left unclear
senses.titleCN: 表述含混：意义没有被说清
senses.definition: the quality of a statement or description that is not precise enough to be understood clearly
senses.definitionCN: 陈述或描述不够精确、因而无法被清楚理解的性质
senses.example: Critics attacked the ambiguity of the policy statement.
senses.exampleCN: 批评者抨击那份政策声明的含混不清。
senses.why: Here the two readings are not both useful; the text simply fails to close the gap. The same fork remains, but it is now a defect of description, recorded from the early 15th century.
senses.whyCN: 这里两种读法并非都有用，文本只是没能把缺口合上。同一个分叉仍在，但此时它是表述上的缺陷；这一用法记录于 15 世纪早期。

senses.title: Two parses of one sentence
senses.titleCN: 同一句话的两种句法切分
senses.definition: in linguistics, the property of a sentence whose grammatical structure can be analysed in more than one way
senses.definitionCN: 在语言学中，指句子的语法结构可以被分析成不止一种形式
senses.example: The sentence 'old men and women' is famous for its structural ambiguity.
senses.exampleCN: “old men and women”这句话以结构歧义著称。
senses.why: The fork is no longer in the dictionary but in the brackets: [old men] and women assigns old to men only, while old [men and women] assigns it to both. One string of words supports two trees.
senses.whyCN: 分叉不在词典里，而在括号里：[old men] and women 把 old 只给 men，而 old [men and women] 把 old 同时给了 men 和 women。同一串词支撑起两棵句法树。

senses.title: Deliberate ambiguity in negotiation
senses.definition: the intentional use of unclear wording so that different parties can each read what they want into it
senses.definitionCN: 故意使用不清楚的措辞，让不同各方都能从中读出自己想要的意思
senses.example: The agreement preserved a deliberate ambiguity over the status of the region.
senses.exampleCN: 该协议在该地区的地位问题上保留了一种有意的含糊。
senses.why: Both readings are kept alive on purpose. Instead of driving the mind to a decision, the wording lets each side drive it in its own direction, so ambiguity becomes a diplomatic tool rather than a fault.
senses.whyCN: 两种读法被有意地同时保留。措辞不把心智驱向某个决定，而是让每一方把它驱向自己的方向，于是含糊从缺陷变成了外交工具。

senses.title: One picture, two figures
senses.definition: the quality of an image or sound that can be perceived in two different ways, as in an ambiguous figure
senses.definitionCN: 图像或声音可以被感知为两种不同样式的性质，如双义图形
senses.example: The duck-rabbit drawing is a classic case of perceptual ambiguity.
senses.exampleCN: 鸭兔图是知觉歧义的经典例子。
senses.why: The eye, like the mind in the earliest sense, is driven to two gestalts and can flip between them. Both readings are fully present in the same stimulus, so neither can be dismissed.
senses.whyCN: 眼睛就像最早义项里的心智，被驱向两种完形，并在两者之间翻转。两种读法都完整地存在于同一个刺激中，因此哪一种都无法被排除。

senses.title: An unclear position or role
senses.definition: the state of having a role or status that is not clearly defined, so that expectations remain unsettled
senses.definitionCN: 所担任的角色或地位没有被清楚界定、因而期待始终悬而未决的状态
senses.example: The ambiguity of her position as adviser and friend caused friction.
senses.exampleCN: 她既是顾问又是朋友，这种身份的模糊引发了摩擦。
senses.why: A person can occupy two categories at once. Neither label wins, so the social situation wavers like the original verb: the same person is legitimately read two ways.
senses.whyCN: 一个人可以同时占据两个类别。两个标签都不占上风，于是社会处境像原动词一样摇摆：同一个人被两种方式合理地解读。

senses.title: Meaning left open in a work
senses.titleCN: 作品中保留的开放意义
senses.definition: in literature and art, the quality of a work that invites several readings without settling on one
senses.definitionCN: 在文学与艺术中，作品邀请多种读法而不落定于其一的品质
senses.example: The ambiguity of the ending is what makes the novel memorable.
senses.exampleCN: 结局的开放含混正是这部小说令人难忘的原因。
senses.why: Here the fork is valued rather than repaired. The work holds two readings in suspension and leaves the reader to waver, turning the old defect into an aesthetic effect.
senses.whyCN: 这里的分叉是被珍视的，而不是被修复的。作品把两种读法悬置起来，让读者自己去摇摆，把旧的缺陷转成了审美效果。

senses.title: Unclear intention behind an act
senses.definition: the quality of an action or gesture whose underlying intention cannot be determined, even when the words or act themselves are clear
senses.definitionCN: 行为或姿态背后的意图无法确定，即使言语或动作本身很清楚
senses.example: There was an ambiguity in his kindness that made her distrust it.
senses.exampleCN: 他的善意里有某种说不清的意味，让她反而起了疑心。
senses.why: Two possible motives are driven at once, so the fork moves from wording to intention. The act is plain, but why it was done remains double, which is why the word can describe motives as well as sentences.
senses.whyCN: 两种可能的动机同时被驱动，分叉就从措辞移到了意图。行为本身很清楚，但“为什么这样做”仍然是双重的；因此这个词既能描述句子，也能描述动机。

intro.en: Ambiguity comes from Latin ambiguitas, a noun of state from ambiguus 'having double meaning'. The verb behind it is ambigere 'to dispute, wander, waver', literally ambi- 'about, both ways' + agere 'to drive'. The second element is therefore agere, not a piece that sounds like 'guity'; the core image is a mind driven in two directions at once.
intro.cn: ambiguity 来自拉丁语 ambiguitas，是由 ambiguus“有两种意思的”构成的状态名词。其背后的动词是 ambigere“争执、徘徊、犹豫”，字面为 ambi-“两边、周围”+ agere“驱动”。因此第二成分是 agere，而不是某个听起来像“guity”的部分；核心意象是心智同时被驱向两个方向。

items.en: First recorded in English as 'uncertainty, doubt, indecision, hesitation', from Old French ambiguite and directly from Latin ambiguitatem (nominative ambiguitas). The earliest sense is about the doubting mind, not about a double-meaning word.
items.cn: 英语最早记录为“不确定、怀疑、犹豫不决”，来自古法语 ambiguite，并直接来自拉丁语 ambiguitatem（主格 ambiguitas）。最早的义项说的是犹豫的心智，而不是一词两义。

items.en: Ambiguitas was a noun of state from ambiguus 'having double meaning, doubtful'. That adjective already contains the fork: a thing can be taken in two ways, and therefore the person facing it does not know which way to go.
items.cn: ambiguitas 是由 ambiguus“有两种意思的、可疑的”构成的状态名词。那个形容词本身已经含有分叉：一件事可以被两种方式理解，因此面对它的人不知道该往哪边走。

items.en: Ambigere meant 'to dispute about, contend, debate', but literally 'to wander, go about, go around', and figuratively 'to hesitate, waver, be in doubt'. The physical image is being driven around in circles rather than arriving at a point.
items.cn: ambigere 意为“就……争执、辩论”，但字面是“游荡、四处走、绕圈”，引申为“犹豫、摇摆、存疑”。其身体意象是被驱赶着绕圈，而不是抵达某一点。

items.en: Ambi- 'about' is from PIE *ambhi- 'around'; agere 'drive, lead, act' is from PIE *ag- 'to drive, draw out or forth, move'. So the word is built on driving, not on any root meaning 'doubt' or 'two-faced'. Ambiguity is what happens when something is driven both ways at once.
items.cn: ambi-“周围”来自原始印欧语 *ambhi-“环绕”；agere“驱动、引领、行动”来自 *ag-“驱赶、拉出、移动”。因此这个词建立在“驱动”上，而不是任何意为“怀疑”或“两面”的词根上。ambiguity 就是某物被同时驱向两边的结果。

items.en: The sense 'obscurity in description' is recorded from the early 15th century. The adjective ambiguous follows later, first attested in Sir Thomas More in 1528, so the abstract noun was in English before its adjective became common.
items.cn: “描述含混”这一义项记录于 15 世纪早期。形容词 ambiguous 出现更晚，最早见于 1528 年的托马斯·莫尔；也就是说，这个抽象名词先进入英语，其形容词后来才通行。

items.en: Modern English extends the same fork to syntax, perception, diplomacy, social roles, art and motive. Two look-alikes must be kept apart: ambivalent is ambi- + valere 'to be worth, be strong', and ambition is ambi- + ire 'to go'. Neither shares the agere element of ambiguity.
items.cn: 现代英语把同一个分叉扩展到句法、知觉、外交、社会角色、艺术与动机。两个形似词必须分开：ambivalent 是 ambi- + valere“有价值、有力量”，ambition 是 ambi- + ire“走”。两者都不含 ambiguity 的 agere 成分。

note.en: The first group separates words that look or sound like ambiguity but are built from different Latin verbs; the second compares words learners often use in its place. The key test is whether the trouble lies in two readings or in missing knowledge.
note.cn: 第一组区分那些形似或音似 ambiguity、却由不同拉丁动词构成的词；第二组比较学习者常用来替换它的词。关键区别是：麻烦究竟来自“两种读法”，还是来自“知识缺失”。

entries.definition: having more than one possible meaning. It is the adjective from ambiguity and names the thing that carries two readings, not the state of doubt itself.
entries.definitionCN: 具有不止一种可能意思的。它是 ambiguity 派生的形容词，指承载两种读法的那个东西，而不是犹疑状态本身。

entries.definition: having mixed or conflicting feelings about someone or something. It is ambi- plus Latin valere 'to be strong, be worth', so it is about two pulls of feeling, not two meanings.
entries.definitionCN: 对某人或某事怀有混合、矛盾的情感。它是 ambi- 加拉丁语 valere“有力量、有价值”，说的是两种情感拉力，而不是两种意思。

entries.definition: a strong desire to achieve something. It goes back to Latin ambire 'to go around', originally canvassing for votes: ambi- + ire 'to go', with no agere.
entries.definitionCN: 实现某事的强烈愿望。它上溯拉丁语 ambire“四处走”，原指为拉票而奔走：ambi- + ire“走”，不含 agere。

entries.definition: relating to walking, or able to walk. It comes from Latin ambulare 'to walk', which merely happens to begin with amb-. There is no ambi- prefix at all.
entries.definitionCN: 与行走有关的，或能行走的。它来自拉丁语 ambulare“行走”，只是碰巧以 amb- 开头，根本没有 ambi- 前缀。

entries.definition: the quality of being imprecise or lacking a clear boundary. Vagueness says the edges are fuzzy; ambiguity says two or more distinct readings are actually available.
entries.definitionCN: 不精确或缺少清晰边界的性质。vagueness 说边界模糊；ambiguity 说确实存在两种或更多彼此不同的读法。

entries.definition: the use of a word with more than one meaning in order to mislead. Equivocation adds the intent to deceive, while ambiguity can be innocent or even useful.
entries.definitionCN: 利用一词多义来误导他人。equivocation 多了一层欺骗意图，而 ambiguity 可以是无意的，甚至是有用的。

entries.definition: the state of not knowing what will happen or what is true. Uncertainty is about the observer's ignorance; ambiguity is about the object supporting several readings.
entries.definitionCN: 不知道会发生什么或什么是真的。uncertainty 说的是观察者的无知；ambiguity 说的是对象本身支持多种读法。

entries.definition: the quality of being hard to understand because it is hidden or unfamiliar. Obscurity hides one meaning; ambiguity displays two.
entries.definitionCN: 因隐蔽或陌生而难以理解的性质。obscurity 把一种意思藏起来；ambiguity 则把两种意思摆出来。

normalIntro.en: Real parts and real relatives: ambi- 'both ways' plus agere 'to drive', the ambiguity family, and the three look-alikes built from valere, ire and ambulare.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分与真实同族词：ambi-“两边”加 agere“驱动”、ambiguity 词族，以及由 valere、ire、ambulare 构成的三个形似词。

normal.en: ambi- means 'both ways' and agere means 'to drive'. Ambiguity is literally a thing driven in two directions at once.
normal.cn: ambi- 意为“两边”，agere 意为“驱动”。ambiguity 字面上就是“被同时驱向两边的状态”。

normal.en: The same agere root gives agent, act, agenda and agile, so ambiguity belongs with 'driving and doing', not with any word for 'two-faced'.
normal.cn: 同一 agere 词根给出 agent、act、agenda、agile，所以 ambiguity 属于“驱动与行动”这一族，与任何“两面”词无关。

normal.en: Three look-alikes use three different second elements: ambivalent has valere 'be worth', ambition has ire 'go', ambulatory has ambulare 'walk'.
normal.cn: 三个形似词用了三个不同的第二成分：ambivalent 是 valere“有价值”，ambition 是 ire“走”，ambulatory 是 ambulare“行走”。

normal.en: The earliest sense was 'hesitation', not 'double meaning'. The mind wavered first; the word's double meaning was named later.
normal.cn: 最早的义项是“犹豫”，不是“一词两义”。先有摇摆的心智，后来才用它命名词语的双重意思。

normal.en: Structural ambiguity lives in brackets: [old men] and women versus old [men and women].
normal.cn: 结构歧义活在括号里：[old men] and women 对 old [men and women]。

abstract.en: Picture a road that splits at a fork. The driver is not lost for lack of a map; both roads are real, and the car is pulled down each one in turn.
abstract.cn: 想象一条在岔口分开的路。司机并非因为没有地图而迷路；两条路都真实存在，车子被先后拉向每一条。

abstract.en: The same fork can sit in a word, a sentence, a drawing, a treaty, a job title or a gesture. What stays constant is that two readings remain standing at once.
abstract.cn: 同一个分叉可以藏在单词、句子、图画、条约、职位名称或一个姿态里。不变的是：两种读法同时立着。

abstract.en: Sometimes the fork is a fault to be repaired; sometimes it is deliberately preserved. Ambiguity can therefore be either a problem or a resource.
abstract.cn: 有时这个分叉是要修掉的缺陷，有时它被有意保留。因此 ambiguity 既可能是问题，也可能是资源。

examples.en: Please rewrite the sentence to remove its ambiguity.
examples.cn: 请改写这句话，消除它的歧义。

examples.en: The play ends in ambiguity, and each audience member decides what happened.
examples.cn: 这部剧以含糊收场，每位观众都自己判断到底发生了什么。

examples.en: There was an ambiguity in her tone that made him unsure whether she was joking.
examples.cn: 她的语气里有某种含混，让他拿不准她是不是在开玩笑。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「俺必鬼题」——俺必答的那道鬼题，两个答案都说得通 → ambiguity 歧义、模棱两可

root: 来自拉丁语 ambiguitas，上溯 ambiguus“有两种意思的”与 ambigere“徘徊、争执”，字面是 ambi-“两边”加 agere“驱动”，核心是“心智被同时驱向两边”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of ambiguity, all one fork: a form, a situation or a mind is driven in two directions at once. Sometimes both readings are legitimate, sometimes the split is a defect, and sometimes it is deliberately preserved.
sensesIntro.cn: ambiguity 的九个义项都源于同一个分叉：一个词形、一种处境或一颗心智被同时驱向两个方向。有时两种读法都合法，有时分裂是缺陷，有时它被有意保留。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one form or situation driven down two roads at the same time.
core.cn: 核心意象：同一个词形或处境被同时驱上两条路。

branches.en: INNER FORK: hesitation and unclear motive. The mind is pulled both ways before any wording is fixed.
branches.cn: 内在分叉：犹豫与动机不明。措辞尚未固定，心智先被拉向两边。

branches.en: CODE: one word or one sentence carries two readings, whether in the dictionary or in the brackets.
branches.cn: 代码层：一个词或一句话承载两种读法，无论在词典里还是在句法括号里。

branches.en: TEXT: vagueness is a fault and open-endedness is a virtue, but both leave meaning unresolved.
branches.cn: 文本层：含混是缺陷，开放是美德，但两者都让意义悬而未决。

branches.en: INSTITUTIONS: negotiators and social roles keep two readings alive, sometimes on purpose and sometimes by accident.
branches.cn: 制度层：谈判者与社会角色让两种读法同时存活，有时出于有意，有时出于无意。

branches.en: PERCEPTION: the eye flips between two figures held in one drawing.
branches.cn: 知觉层：眼睛在一张图里所持的两个形象之间翻转。

intro.en: Ambiguity is a Latin-derived noun whose parts are frozen: ambi- 'both ways' + agere 'to drive' + -ity. English adds only ordinary suffixes to the finished family. The -ity is not a meaning-bearing 'guity' chunk, and the whole word never meant 'two-faced'.
intro.cn: ambiguity 是拉丁来源的名词，其成分已经凝固：ambi-“两边”+ agere“驱动”+ -ity。英语只是在成品词族后加普通后缀。-ity 并不是一个带意义的“guity”部件，整个词也从来不是“两面派”的意思。

latinIntro.en: The Latin family is ambigere 'to dispute, wander, waver', its adjective ambiguus 'double-meaning, doubtful', and agere 'to drive, lead, act'. The same agere yields agent, act, agenda and agile, while ambivalent and ambition belong to valere and ire respectively.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词族包括 ambigere“争执、徘徊、犹豫”、其形容词 ambiguus“有两种意思的、可疑的”，以及 agere“驱动、引领、行动”。同一 agere 给出 agent、act、agenda、agile，而 ambivalent 与 ambition 分别属于 valere 和 ire。

items.structure: ambi- (both ways) + agere (to drive) + -ity (noun of state)
items.meaning: the state of being driven two ways, hence double meaning or doubt
items.meaningCN: 被驱向两边的状态，因而指歧义或犹疑（-ity 构成状态名词）
items.example: The ambiguity of the clause delayed the signing.
items.exampleCN: 条款的歧义推迟了签署。

items.meaning: open to more than one interpretation
items.meaningCN: 可作不止一种解释的；有歧义的（-ous 构成形容词）
items.example: He gave an ambiguous answer and left the room.
items.exampleCN: 他给了个模棱两可的回答，然后离开了房间。

items.meaning: in a way that can be understood in more than one sense
items.meaningCN: 以含糊、可作多种理解的方式（-ly 构成方式副词）
items.example: She smiled ambiguously and said nothing.
items.exampleCN: 她含义不明地笑了笑，什么也没说。

items.meaningCN: 有歧义性；含糊（-ness 构成性质名词）
items.example: The ambiguousness of the title was intentional.
items.exampleCN: 标题的含混是有意为之。

items.meaningCN: 不含糊的；只有一种清楚意思的（un- 否定）
items.example: The instructions were short and unambiguous.
items.exampleCN: 说明简短而明确。

items.meaning: in a way that leaves no doubt
items.meaningCN: 毫不含糊地；明确无误地
items.example: The court ruled unambiguously in her favour.
items.exampleCN: 法院明确无误地判她胜诉。

items.structure: ambi- (both) + valere (to be worth, be strong) — a different root
items.meaning: having mixed feelings; not the same as having two meanings
items.meaningCN: 有矛盾情感的；与“两种意思”不同源（valere 有价值、有力量）
items.example: She felt ambivalent about moving abroad.
items.exampleCN: 她对移居国外心情矛盾。

items.meaning: the state of having conflicting feelings
items.meaningCN: 矛盾情感；正反情绪并存（-ence 构成状态名词）
items.example: His ambivalence made the decision harder.
items.exampleCN: 他的矛盾心理让决定更难做。

items.structure: ambi- (around) + ire (to go) — a different root
items.meaning: a strong drive to achieve something, originally 'going around' to canvass
items.meaningCN: 雄心；抱负（原指四处奔走拉票，与 agere 无关）
items.example: Her ambition was to lead the research team.
items.exampleCN: 她的抱负是领导这个研究团队。

items.structure: ambi- (around) + ire (to go) — a different root
items.meaning: the scope or boundary of something
items.meaningCN: 范围；界限（同 ambire 一族，与 agere 无关）
items.example: That question lies outside the ambit of the inquiry.
items.exampleCN: 那个问题不在调查范围之内。

latinEntries.meaning: to dispute, wander, waver, be in doubt

definition_zh: 权威的；经典的；规范的；正宗的；教规的
definition_en: conforming to accepted, authoritative standards; belonging to an official list of works; also relating to church law
core_image: 一列被正式批准的书单摆在架子上：凡在单内的才算正宗
scene: 文学系的走廊里，墙上贴着必修书单，学生们按单购书。 Moby-Dick is canonical reading in every American literature course.
sceneCN: 这里 canonical 是「经典的、正典的」（第 2 个义项：列入权威书目的）；句意是《白鲸》是美国文学课程的必读经典。

pos.zh: 权威的；经典的；正宗的
规范的；标准形式的（数学、逻辑）
教规的；按教会法的

derivatives.zh: 基础名词，义为「正典；准则；教规；（音乐）卡农」
由形容词加动词化后缀构成，义为「使规范化；转为标准形式」（技术用语）
由形容词加副词后缀构成，义为「按正典地；以标准形式」
同根宗教用语，义为「封圣；列入正典」

senses.title: Belonging to the official or accepted list
senses.definition: included in the authoritative canon of works, scriptures, or facts regarded as genuine
senses.definitionCN: 属于被认定为正宗的权威书目、经卷或事实范围之内
senses.example: Fans debate whether the sequel is canonical or side material.
senses.exampleCN: 粉丝们争论这部续作属于正史还是衍生设定。
senses.why: The canon is the measuring rod: what fits the rod is genuine, what does not is excluded.
senses.whyCN: canon 本义是量杆：合乎量杆者为真，不合者出局。

senses.title: Widely recognized as excellent or standard
senses.definition: regarded as a standard of excellence that educated people are expected to know
senses.definitionCN: 被视为卓越标准、受过教育者理应知晓的
senses.example: Her early papers are canonical in the field.
senses.exampleCN: 她早期的论文是该领域的经典之作。
senses.why: Repeated inclusion in lists and syllabi makes a work part of the measuring rod itself.
senses.whyCN: 反复入选书目与课程，作品便化身为量杆本身。

senses.title: Expressed in the standard form
senses.titleCN: 标准形式的；规范形的（数学、逻辑、技术）
senses.definition: written or expressed in the simplest or most standard form agreed by convention
senses.definitionCN: 按约定以最简或最标准的形式书写或表达
senses.example: Reduce the equation to its canonical form.
senses.exampleCN: 把这个方程化成标准形。
senses.why: Once a rule exists, every case is rewritten until it matches the rule exactly.
senses.whyCN: 规则一旦确立，所有情形都要改写至与规则完全一致。

senses.title: Relating to church law or order
senses.definition: governed by or belonging to the regulations of a church
senses.definitionCN: 受教会法规约束的，或属于教会法规的
senses.example: The canonical age for priesthood was once twenty-four.
senses.exampleCN: 过去担任神父的法定教会年龄是二十四岁。
senses.why: Church councils wrote their rules as canons, the rod that measures the faithful.
senses.whyCN: 教会会议以「教规」（canon）形式立法，即度量信众的量杆。

intro.en: Canonical is built on Greek kanōn, a straight rod or rule, which became both the church's law list and literature's list of approved works.
intro.cn: canonical 建立在希腊语 kanōn（直杆、准则）之上，这个词既成为教会的法规目录，也成了文学的正典书目。

items.en: The root *ken- is associated with a reed or straight stick used for measuring.
items.cn: 词根 *ken- 与用作量具的芦苇或直棍相关。

items.en: Greek kanōn meant a rod, rule, or standard of measurement, then any guiding principle.
items.cn: 希腊语 kanōn 指量杆、规矩，进而指一切指导性准则。

items.en: Latin canon carried the rule sense and, in church use, the list of accepted scriptures.
items.cn: 拉丁语 canon 保留「准则」义，在教会用法中指被接受的经卷目录。

items.en: English took canon for church law early, and by the seventeenth century canonical described whatever conformed to it.
items.cn: 英语早期以 canon 指教会法规，至十七世纪 canonical 形容符合法规的一切事物。

items.en: Modern usage extends from scripture to literature, mathematics, physics, and pop-culture continuity.
items.cn: 现代用法从经卷扩展到文学、数学、物理学乃至流行文化的设定体系。

note.en: Canonical keeps close company with its base canon and with words for official standards.
note.cn: canonical 与词基 canon 联系紧密，并与一系列「官方标准」词汇相邻。

entries.definitionCN: 正典、准则、公认作品总目；亦指音乐中的卡农。

entries.definition: A large gun; one letter from canon but unrelated in origin.
entries.definitionCN: 大炮，与 canon 仅差一个字母，词源无关。

entries.definitionCN: 封圣；把作品列入正典。

entries.definition: To convert data into its standard form, a computing usage.
entries.definitionCN: 把数据转换为标准形式，计算技术用语。

entries.definition: Accepted as true and reliable because of official standing.
entries.definitionCN: 因官方地位而被视为真实可靠的权威说法。

entries.definition: Conforming to the accepted traditional belief or practice.
entries.definitionCN: 恪守正统信仰或做法的。

entries.definition: Serving as the usual or expected model.
entries.definitionCN: 作为通行或预期范本的。

entries.definition: Of doubtful authenticity, excluded from the accepted list.
entries.definitionCN: 真伪存疑的、被排除在正典之外的，与 canonical 相对。

entries.definition: Strongly influential in later development, often applied to founding works.
entries.definitionCN: 对后续发展影响深远的，常指奠基之作。

normalIntro.cn: 五条围绕「量杆」词根与「钦定书目」意象的记忆钩子。

normal.en: Root picture: Greek kanōn is a straight rod, the original ruler of standards.
normal.cn: 词根画面：希腊语 kanōn 是一根直杆，最初的「标准之尺」。

normal.en: Church lane: canonical hours are the fixed prayer times of monastic life.
normal.cn: 教会一线：canonical hours 是修道生活的固定祈祷时辰。

normal.en: Math lane: canonical form names the agreed simplest version of an equation or matrix.
normal.cn: 数学一线：canonical form 指方程或矩阵约定的最简标准形。

normal.en: Fandom lane: in serialized stories, canonical means part of the true, official plot.
normal.cn: 粉丝圈一线：在连载故事里，canonical 意为属于官方正史剧情。

abstract.cn: 木匠的水平尺逐一抵住书架上的书，稍有倾斜便被滑落出局。

abstract.en: A golden list nailed to the temple door, rewritten only by council.
abstract.cn: 一张钉在圣殿门上的金字名录，唯有公议才能改写。

abstract.en: Every road in the town repainted until it matches the one official map.
abstract.cn: 全镇道路一再重画，直到与唯一一张官方地图完全吻合。

examples.cn: 这位教授偏好该作曲家作品目录的正统编年。

examples.en: Engineers store the data in canonical form to avoid duplicate records.
examples.cn: 工程师以规范形式存储数据，以避免重复记录。

examples.en: The novel quickly became canonical despite mixed early reviews.
examples.cn: 尽管早期评价毁誉参半，这部小说很快成为经典。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「克脑你扣」——审核者敲着脑壳要求你扣紧标准答案，不合规范就打回，正是「权威的、规范的」；联想教会里被敲定的正经书单。

root: 源自希腊语 kanōn（直杆、量尺、准则），经拉丁语 canon（准则；教会法规；正典书目）进入英语，加形容词后缀 -ical 构成 canonical。词根一般认为出自指芦苇、直棍的印欧词根 *ken-。同根词有 canonize（封圣）、canonicalize（规范化）；注意与「大炮」cannon 词源无关。

sensesIntro.en: From the measuring rod the word covers the official list, the standard of excellence, the normalized form, and church law.
sensesIntro.cn: 从量杆出发，词义涵盖钦定名录、卓越标准、规范化形式与教会法规。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a straight rod laid against everything to see what measures up.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根直杆抵住万物，量出何者合格。

branches.en: THE SHELF: what the official list includes and excludes.
branches.cn: 书架：官方名录的收录与除名。

branches.en: THE SYLLABUS: works everyone educated is expected to know.
branches.cn: 课程表：受过教育者理应知晓的作品。

branches.en: THE BLACKBOARD: equations rewritten into their one agreed shape.
branches.cn: 黑板：方程被改写为约定的唯一形态。

branches.en: THE CLOISTER: church law governing hours, ages, and offices.
branches.cn: 修道院：约束时辰、年龄与圣职的教会法。

branches.en: THE COMMON LOGIC: in both canons and forms, deviation means exclusion.
branches.cn: 共通逻辑：无论正典还是标准形，偏离即出局。

intro.en: Canonical is canon plus the adjective suffix -ical, literally of the rod, of the rule.
intro.cn: canonical 由 canon 加形容词后缀 -ical 构成，字面即「属于量杆的、属于准则的」。

latinIntro.en: The kanōn root feeds church law, music, mathematics, and the bookshelf all at once.
latinIntro.cn: kanōn 词根同时滋养了教会法、音乐、数学与书架。

definition_zh: 人类学研究；以田野与比较方法对某一人类社会或文化所作的专题研究
definition_en: a research project or published account that examines a human society or culture by anthropological methods
core_image: 一间借住的屋子、一叠按日期编号的笔记、一张把几个社会并排画出的比较表
scene: 书架最上层放着一叠关于同一座村庄的报告，年份不同，封面却几乎一样。 Her anthropological study of the village began with a question about names.
sceneCN: 这里「人类学研究」指一项以田野与比较为方法的专题研究（第 1 个义项：作为研究项目）；句意为她对这座村庄的人类学研究始于一个关于姓名的问题。

pos.zh: 人类学研究（可数，指一项研究或一份成果；复数 anthropological studies）

collocations.zh: 一项经典的人类学研究
关于亲属关系的人类学研究
关于仪式的人类学研究

derivatives.zh: anthropo-（希腊「人」）+ -logy（希腊「学问」）→ 人类学：这项研究所属的学科
拉丁 studium「热忱、钻研」经古法语 estudie → 研究；学习（语义偏移：从「热心」到「用心的成果」）
拉丁 studere「用心」的现在分词名词化 → 学生（语义偏移：正在用心的人）
studium + -ous（充满）→ 好学的（语义偏移：以用心为特征）

senses.title: A research project
senses.titleCN: 作为研究项目：有计划地追问一个问题
senses.definition: a planned inquiry into one society or culture, with a question and a design
senses.definitionCN: 针对某一社会或文化、带着问题与设计的有计划考察
senses.example: Her anthropological study of the village began with a question about names.
senses.exampleCN: 她对这座村庄的人类学研究始于一个关于姓名的问题。
senses.why: Study came from Latin studium, 'eager application', so the phrase names an application of the mind to a case; anthropological says which instruments the application uses.
senses.whyCN: study 出自拉丁 studium「热忱、钻研」，因此这个短语指心智对某个案例的用心；anthropological 则说明用的是哪套仪器。

senses.title: The published account
senses.titleCN: 作为成果：写成书或论文的那一份
senses.definition: the book or article in which the inquiry is finally set out
senses.definitionCN: 研究最终写成的书或论文
senses.example: The anthropological study appeared eight years after the last field visit.
senses.exampleCN: 这项人类学研究在最后一次田野访问八年之后出版。
senses.why: In academic English a study often means the document rather than the doing: what is cited in a footnote is the printed result, not the years behind it.
senses.whyCN: 在学术英语里，study 常指文献而非活动：脚注里引用的是印出来的结果，而不是它背后的那些年。

senses.title: The fieldwork itself
senses.titleCN: 作为田野活动：住在当地做观察的过程
senses.definition: the activity of living among people and observing their daily life
senses.definitionCN: 住在当地人中间观察其日常生活的活动
senses.example: The anthropological study required two years of learning the local verb forms.
senses.exampleCN: 这项人类学研究需要两年时间去学当地的动词形式。
senses.why: Residence is the discipline's instrument, and study can name the instrument's use: the long stay is the study, before anything is written.
senses.whyCN: 驻留是这门学科的仪器，study 可以指仪器的使用：在写成文字之前，那段长住就是研究。

senses.title: A comparative investigation
senses.titleCN: 作为比较：把多个案例并排放
senses.definition: an inquiry that sets several cases side by side in order to compare them
senses.definitionCN: 把若干案例并置以便比较的考察
senses.example: Their anthropological study compared burial customs in four river valleys.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的人类学研究比较了四条河谷的丧葬习俗。
senses.why: Comparison is what turns a description into anthropology; a single case can be described, but a study in this sense needs at least two.
senses.whyCN: 比较才把描述变成人类学；单一案例可以被描述，但此义上的研究至少需要两个案例。

senses.title: A long-term community study
senses.titleCN: 作为长期跟踪：隔年回访同一社区
senses.definition: a repeated inquiry into one community over many years or decades
senses.definitionCN: 在多年乃至数十年间反复回访同一社区的考察
senses.example: The anthropological study returned to the same households in three different decades.
senses.exampleCN: 这项人类学研究在三个不同年代回访了同一批家庭。
senses.why: Because social life changes slowly and unevenly, only repetition over time can show what is stable and what is passing; the phrase then denotes a series rather than one visit.
senses.whyCN: 社会生活变得缓慢而不均匀，只有跨时间的重复才能显出什么稳定、什么短暂；此时短语指一个系列，而非一次访问。

senses.title: A method-defined study
senses.titleCN: 按方法界定：以参与观察为核心的研究
senses.definition: a study defined by participant observation rather than by survey or experiment
senses.definitionCN: 以参与观察、而非问卷或实验来界定的研究
senses.example: The anthropological study was judged by its method, not only by its findings.
senses.exampleCN: 这项人类学研究是按其方法、而不只按结论来评判的。
senses.why: The adjective can attach to the method rather than the field: work is anthropological when it was done by living there, whatever its subject.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词可以附在方法上而非学科上：只要靠住在那里完成，不论题目是什么，工作就是人类学的。

senses.title: A branch-specific study
senses.titleCN: 属于某一分支：如生物人类学的研究
senses.definition: an inquiry located in one branch, such as biological or linguistic work
senses.definitionCN: 位于生物、语言等某一分支之内的考察
senses.example: A biological anthropological study measured growth in the same children each year.
senses.exampleCN: 一项生物人类学研究每年测量同一批儿童的生长。
senses.why: Once the four fields split, the phrase needed qualifying adjectives; the branch name tells you which instruments were used and which evidence counts.
senses.whyCN: 四分支分开之后，这个短语需要限定形容词；分支名告诉你用了哪些仪器、哪种证据才算数。

senses.title: A commissioned study
senses.titleCN: 受委托的研究：为机构解决具体问题
senses.definition: a study paid for by an institution to answer a practical question
senses.definitionCN: 由机构出资、为回答实际问题而做的研究
senses.example: The ministry commissioned an anthropological study of why the clinic went unused.
senses.exampleCN: 该部门委托做一项人类学研究，追问诊所为何无人使用。
senses.why: Study can be bought: a client pays for a question and a report, and the same methods serve a decision rather than a discipline.
senses.whyCN: 研究可以被购买：委托方付钱买一个问题与一份报告，同样的方法服务于决策，而非学科。

intro.en: The phrase joins a Greek-derived field adjective to a Latin-derived noun for eager application; the noun's history is plain, the Greek stem's is not.
intro.cn: 这个短语把希腊来源的学科形容词接在拉丁来源的「用心」名词上；名词的历史清楚，希腊词干则不然。

items.en: Anthropos 'human being' is well attested, but its internal analysis is disputed; the reading as aner 'man' plus ops 'face' is a hypothesis, not a demonstrated derivation.
items.cn: anthropos「人」书证充分，但内部构造有争议；读作 anēr「男人」加 ōps「脸」只是假说，并非已证实的派生。

items.en: -Logia 'account, study' derives from logos 'word, reason' and legein 'to gather, say'; the deeper Indo-European root is reconstructed.
items.cn: -logia「叙述、学问」出自 logos「言词、理性」与 legein「收集、说出」；更深的印欧词根为重构。

items.en: Studium meant 'eagerness, application, pursuit of knowledge', from studere 'to be eager for'. The verb's origin is not settled beyond Latin, and any earlier form is a reconstruction.
items.cn: studium 意为「热忱、用心、求知的 pursuit」，来自 studere「热衷于」。该动词在拉丁语之前来源未定，更早的形式均为重构。

items.en: Old French estudie carried the noun into English in the thirteenth century, first as the state of being eager, then as the object pursued.
items.cn: 古法语 estudie 在 13 世纪把这个名词带入英语，先指用心的状态，后指所钻研的对象。

items.en: The combination with anthropological is a nineteenth-century product: the field needed a countable noun for one piece of work, and study supplied it.
items.cn: 与 anthropological 的组合是 19 世纪的产物：这门学科需要一个可数的名词来指一件具体工作，study 正好补上。

items.en: Source uncertain: the exact phrase has no fixed first citation, the make-up of anthropos is unsettled, and the pre-Latin origin of studere is unknown.
items.cn: 来源不确定：这一确切短语没有公认的最早书证；anthropos 的构造无定论；studere 在拉丁语之前的来源不明。

note.en: Group one holds near-identical phrases and words that are routinely substituted; group two holds the kinds of writing a study turns into.
note.cn: 第一组是常被直接替换的近形短语与单词；第二组是研究会变成的几种文字成品。

entries.definition: The activity of collecting data among people; a study is what that activity eventually makes.
entries.definitionCN: 在人群中收集资料的活动；研究是这项活动最终做出的东西。

entries.definition: The written description of one people, often the form an anthropological study takes.
entries.definitionCN: 对单一族群的文字描述，常是人类学研究所采取的形式。

entries.definition: An intensive inquiry into a single instance; it needs no fieldwork and belongs to no particular discipline.
entries.definitionCN: 对单一实例的深入考察；不必田野，也不专属某一学科。

entries.definition: A study that asks fixed questions of many people at once, rather than living among a few.
entries.definitionCN: 一次向许多人提出固定问题的研究，而非住在少数人中间。

entries.definition: A book-length treatment of one subject; the usual final shape of a long study.
entries.definitionCN: 对单一主题的整书篇幅处理；长期研究的常见最终形态。

entries.definition: A short published report of findings, narrower and faster than a monograph.
entries.definitionCN: 较短的研究成果发表形式，比专著更窄更快。

entries.definition: A formal account prepared for an institution, often the product of a commissioned study.
entries.definitionCN: 为机构准备的正式陈述，常是受委托研究的成品。

entries.definition: The long research text that earns a doctorate, usually the first big study a practitioner completes.
entries.definitionCN: 为取得博士学位而写的长篇研究文本，通常是从业者完成的第一项大研究。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real genre names and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实文体名与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: anthropos 'human' + logia 'study' + studium 'eager application': an eager application of the discipline to one case.
normal.cn: anthropos「人」+ logia「学问」+ studium「用心」：把学问用心地施于一个案例。

normal.en: A study is first a doing, then a document; the phrase can mean either, which is why citations sound like objects.
normal.cn: 研究先是活动，后是文献；短语两义兼有，所以引文里听起来像物件。

normal.en: The family runs study, student, studious, anthropology, anthropological, ethnography.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 study、student、studious、anthropology、anthropological、ethnography。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: conduct a study, publish a study, a long-term study.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：开展研究、发表研究、长期研究。

normal.en: Shape check: question, design, residence, notes, comparison, account.
normal.cn: 结构检查：问题、设计、驻留、笔记、比较、成文。

abstract.en: Picture a shelf where ten reports about one village stand in a row like years on a ruler.
abstract.cn: 想象书架上一排关于同一村庄的报告，像尺子上的年份。

abstract.en: Picture a notebook that grows heavier than the suitcase it travelled in.
abstract.cn: 想象一本笔记比它随行的箱子还重。

abstract.en: Picture a footnote pointing to a book that took longer to write than the building it is stored in.
abstract.cn: 想象一条脚注指向一本书，写它花的时间比存放它的楼还久。

examples.en: The anthropological study was rejected by two journals before it changed the field.
examples.cn: 这项人类学研究被两家期刊拒绝，后来却改变了这个领域。

examples.en: Students read an anthropological study of a market and then visit one.
examples.cn: 学生先读一份关于市场的人类学研究，再去逛一个市场。

examples.en: A good anthropological study says how the researcher changed the place being studied.
examples.cn: 好的人类学研究会说清研究者如何改变了被研究的地方。

dict_mnemonic.text: anthropo（人）+ logical（学问的）+ study（研究）＝ 用人类学方法做的一项研究；记「先住进去，再并排比较，最后成书」。

root: 希腊 anthrōpos「人」+ -logia「学问」构成学科形容词；拉丁 studium「热忱、钻研」（来自 studere）经古法语 estudie 构成 study。anthropos 与 studere 的更深来源均不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one piece of work from question to print: the project, the book, the residence, the comparison, the decades of return visits, the method that defines it, the branch it belongs to and the client who paid for it.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项跟着同一件工作从提问走到付印：项目、成书、驻留、比较、数十年的回访、界定它的方法、它所属的分支，以及出钱的委托方。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a borrowed room, a numbered notebook and a comparison table of several societies on one page.
core.cn: 核心意象：一间借住的屋子、一叠编号的笔记，以及一页并排画出几个社会的比较表。

branches.en: BEFORE AND AFTER PRINT: the planned inquiry, then the document that outlives it.
branches.cn: 付印前后：先是计划中的考察，后是比它活得更久的文献。

branches.en: THE INSTRUMENT AND ITS RULE: living there, and the method that makes living there count as evidence.
branches.cn: 仪器与其规则：住在那里，以及使这段居住成为证据的方法。

branches.en: TWO AXES OF COMPARISON: several cases side by side, and one case followed across decades.
branches.cn: 比较的两轴：多个案例并排，以及一个案例跨越数十年。

branches.en: THE BRANCH LABEL: the qualifying adjective decides which instruments and which evidence.
branches.cn: 分支标签：限定形容词决定用哪些仪器、认哪种证据。

branches.en: THE CLIENT: a paid question turns the same method toward a decision.
branches.cn: 委托方：付费的问题把同一套方法转向一个决策。

intro.en: The phrase is a Greek compound adjective plus a Latin noun, so two different morphological systems meet in one term.
intro.cn: 这个短语是希腊复合形容词加拉丁名词，两套构词系统在一个术语里相遇。

latinIntro.en: Greek anthropos and -logia build the adjective; Latin studium builds the noun, and the Latin noun family is the one that grew in English.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 anthropos 与 -logia 构成形容词；拉丁 studium 构成名词，而英语中长大的是拉丁名词词族。

items.example: The anthropo- element also builds anthropoid.
items.exampleCN: anthropo- 也构成 anthropoid。

items.example: The suffix is shared with biology.
items.exampleCN: 该后缀与 biology 共用。

items.example: The ending makes a relational adjective from the field name.
items.exampleCN: 该词尾把学科名变成关系形容词。

items.example: The Latin noun names the mental effort behind the work.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁名词指工作背后的心力。

items.meaning: a piece of research; to inquire
items.example: The noun and the verb share one Latin source.
items.exampleCN: 名词与动词共享同一个拉丁来源。

items.meaning: one who applies himself to learning
items.example: The ending marks the person in the act of applying.
items.exampleCN: 该词尾标记正处于用功状态的人。

items.example: The adjective describes the habit, not the project.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词描述习惯，而非项目。

items.example: Ethnography is the genre a study often becomes.
items.exampleCN: 民族志常是研究最终变成的文体。

items.example: The adjective limits which methods count.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词限定哪些方法算数。

latinEntries.structure: anthropologia, -ae (New Latin, f., first declension, from Greek)

latinEntries.meaning: to be eager for, apply oneself

definition_zh: 研究者；科研人员；调查者；调研员；学术研究者
definition_en: a person whose job is to study a subject carefully in order to discover new facts or reach a judgement
core_image: 深夜的档案室里，一个人把三十年前的借阅卡一张张摊开，用铅笔在笔记本上画出时间线。
scene: 出版社编辑等这位作者交稿等了两年，因为他把每一份旧报纸都翻过一遍，才敢写下那一段历史。 A careful researcher, he read every old newspaper before writing that chapter.
sceneCN: 这里 researcher 是“从事系统研究的人”（第 1 个义项）；句意：他靠反复查证原始材料来完成研究。

pos.zh: 研究者；科研人员；调查者

senses.title: Someone who studies systematically
senses.titleCN: 研究者：系统地查证一个问题的人
senses.definition: a person who investigates a subject in a planned, systematic way
senses.definitionCN: 以有计划、系统的方式探究某个主题的人
senses.example: The researcher spent four years tracking the same herd.
senses.exampleCN: 这位研究者花了四年追踪同一群动物。
senses.why: The agent suffix -er marks the person who performs the action named by research, and research literally means searching again and again.
senses.whyCN: 施事后缀 -er 标记执行 research 这一动作的人，而 research 字面上就是“反复搜寻”。

senses.title: An investigator of facts
senses.titleCN: 调查者：把事实一层层挖出来的人
senses.definition: a person who digs out facts, especially for a report or an inquiry
senses.definitionCN: 把事实层层挖出的人，尤指为报道或调查
senses.example: The researcher found the missing invoice in a county archive.
senses.exampleCN: 这位调查者在县档案馆找到了那张失踪的发票。
senses.why: Research began as intensive searching, so the person sense covers reporters and investigators, not only scientists.
senses.whyCN: research 本义是密集搜寻，因此这个指人的义项也覆盖记者与调查员，而不只是科学家。

senses.title: A member of a lab or university
senses.titleCN: 科研人员：实验室与大学里的研究者
senses.definition: a scientist or scholar employed to carry out academic or laboratory research
senses.definitionCN: 受雇从事学术或实验室研究的科学家或学者
senses.example: Two researchers in the lab share the microscopy work.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室里的两名科研人员分担显微观察工作。
senses.why: Institutions turn the activity into a post, and the post gives the word its most common occupational sense.
senses.whyCN: 机构把这项活动变成岗位，而岗位赋予这个词最常见的职业含义。

senses.title: A clinical investigator
senses.titleCN: 临床研究员：在病人身上验证疗法的人
senses.definition: someone who runs or assists medical studies with human participants
senses.definitionCN: 主持或协助以人为对象的医学研究的人
senses.example: The clinical researcher explained the trial to each volunteer.
senses.exampleCN: 临床研究员向每位志愿者解释了试验内容。
senses.why: When the field is medicine, the search is for safety and effect in people, so the same title carries ethical duties.
senses.whyCN: 当领域是医学时，所搜寻的是药物在人身上的安全与效果，因此同一头衔也带着伦理责任。

senses.title: A market or survey analyst
senses.titleCN: 调研员：用问卷和数据摸清市场的人
senses.definition: a person who designs surveys or studies consumers for a company
senses.definitionCN: 为公司设计问卷或研究消费者的人
senses.example: The market researcher ran focus groups before the launch.
senses.exampleCN: 市场调研员在产品发布前组织了焦点小组。
senses.why: Commercial research also searches, but its object is preference and demand rather than natural law.
senses.whyCN: 商业研究同样在搜寻，但对象是偏好与需求，而不是自然规律。

senses.title: Someone working outside institutions
senses.titleCN: 独立研究者：不隶属机构的学者
senses.definition: a scholar who pursues research without a university or company post
senses.definitionCN: 不在大学或公司任职而从事研究的学者
senses.example: An independent researcher corrected the census transcription.
senses.exampleCN: 一位独立研究者更正了那次人口普查的转录。
senses.why: The word names the activity, not the employer; removing the institution leaves the searching intact.
senses.whyCN: 这个词命名的是活动而非雇主；去掉机构，搜寻这件事依然完整。

senses.title: A digger in archives
senses.titleCN: 史料研究者：在档案堆里找证据的人
senses.definition: a person whose method is the close reading of documents, records, and manuscripts
senses.definitionCN: 以细读文件、记录与手稿为方法的人
senses.example: The historian works as a researcher in the national library.
senses.exampleCN: 这位历史学家在国家图书馆做史料研究。
senses.why: Documents are a second kind of field: evidence is buried in paper, and finding it is still a search.
senses.whyCN: 文献是另一种田野：证据埋在纸堆里，把它找出来仍然是搜寻。

senses.title: A student learning the craft
senses.titleCN: 研究生研究者：边学边做的年轻学者
senses.definition: a graduate student or junior member learning to conduct research within a team
senses.definitionCN: 在团队中边学习边开展研究的研究生或初级成员
senses.example: Each researcher presents her findings at the weekly seminar.
senses.exampleCN: 每位研究生研究者都在每周讨论会上报告自己的发现。
senses.why: Training and research merge in the modern laboratory, so the title also covers those still learning the method.
senses.whyCN: 现代实验室里训练与研究合而为一，因此这个头衔也覆盖仍在学习方法的人。

intro.en: Researcher is research plus -er. Research is re- plus search, and search goes back through Old French cerchier to Latin circare, to go about, from circus, a circle.
intro.cn: researcher 由 research 加 -er 构成。research 是 re- 加 search，而 search 经古法语 cerchier 上溯到拉丁语 circare“四处走动”，其词源为 circus“圆圈”。

items.en: Circus meant a ring or circle. The round track supplied the image of going round and round a space.
items.cn: circus 意为“圆圈、环”。环形跑道提供了“绕着某处来回走”的形象。

items.en: Circare meant to go about or wander over an area. Searching is pictured as walking a territory until nothing is missed.
items.cn: circare 意为在某区域内走动、巡行。搜寻被想象成把一片地方走遍，直到没有遗漏。

items.en: Old French cerchier meant to search or seek, keeping the image of circling a place to find something.
items.cn: 古法语 cerchier 意为搜寻、寻找，保留了“绕着某处转以找到东西”的形象。

items.en: Middle French recerche meant a close search, with re- adding intensity or repetition rather than simple return.
items.cn: 中古法语 recerche 意为仔细搜寻，其中的 re- 加强的是强度或反复，而不只是“返回”。

items.en: English research first meant the act of searching closely; only later did it become the systematic study of a subject.
items.cn: 英语 research 最初指仔细搜寻的行为，后来才指对某一主题的系统研究。

items.en: The Old English agent suffix -ere became -er, marking the person who performs the action of the verb.
items.cn: 古英语施事后缀 -ere 演变为 -er，标记执行动词动作的人。

note.en: The first group is the research family, separated by word class; the second compares people who investigate in different settings.
note.cn: 第一组是 research 词族，按词类区分；第二组比较在不同场景中从事调查的人。

entries.definition: systematic investigation of a subject. It names the activity or the body of work.
entries.definitionCN: 对某主题的系统研究；命名的是活动或成果。

entries.definition: able to be investigated with available methods and evidence.
entries.definitionCN: 能够用现有方法与证据加以研究的。

entries.definition: carefully investigated, as in a well-researched article. It judges the finished product.
entries.definitionCN: 经过仔细研究的，如“研究扎实的文章”；评判的是成品。

entries.definition: a person who investigates, especially a crime or an official inquiry. It stresses uncovering causes.
entries.definitionCN: 从事调查的人，尤指刑事案件或官方调查；强调查明原因。

entries.definition: a person with deep learning in a field. It stresses knowledge rather than the process of discovery.
entries.definitionCN: 在某一领域学识深厚的人；强调学识而非发现过程。

entries.definition: a person who examines data or situations to explain them. It stresses interpretation.
entries.definitionCN: 分析数据或形势以作出解释的人；强调解读。

entries.definition: a person trained in a natural or social science. It names a profession rather than an activity.
entries.definitionCN: 受过自然科学或社会科学训练的人；命名的是职业而非活动。

normalIntro.en: Real parts only: re-, search, -er. Search itself comes from a Latin verb for going round a place, so a researcher is someone who keeps walking the territory.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分：re-、search、-er。search 出自拉丁语中“绕行某地”的动词，因此研究者就是反复走遍这片地方的人。

normal.en: Re plus search plus er: the person who searches again and again.
normal.cn: re 加 search 加 er：一遍又一遍搜寻的那个人。

normal.en: Search comes from circling a field until nothing is missed.
normal.cn: search 出自绕着田野走遍、直到没有遗漏。

normal.en: A researcher in an archive is walking a paper field.
normal.cn: 在档案馆里的研究者，是在一片纸做的田野上行走。

normal.en: The -er tells you who; the research tells you what they keep doing.
normal.cn: 词尾告诉你“谁”，词根告诉你“他一直在做什么”。

normal.en: A clinical researcher searches for safety in people, not in test tubes.
normal.cn: 临床研究员在人身上寻找安全性，而不是在试管里。

abstract.en: Research is only called systematic when the searcher can say where the search stopped.
abstract.cn: 只有当搜寻者说得出自己在哪里停下时，研究才被称为系统的。

abstract.en: Every researcher chooses a small field to walk, and the choice is already an argument.
abstract.cn: 每位研究者都选一小片田野去走，而这个选择本身已是一种主张。

abstract.en: The word keeps its old image: knowledge is produced by circling a question long enough.
abstract.cn: 这个词保留着旧形象：知识是靠围绕一个问题转得足够久才产生的。

examples.en: Researchers at three universities compared the same soil samples.
examples.cn: 三所大学的研究者比较了同一批土壤样本。

examples.en: As a researcher, she is known for checking every citation by hand.
examples.cn: 作为研究者，她以逐条手工核对引文而闻名。

examples.en: The market researcher found that shoppers ignored the new labels.
examples.cn: 市场调研员发现购物者根本不看新标签。

dict_mnemonic.text: re（反复）+ search（搜寻）+ er（人）——反复搜寻的人，就是研究者。

root: 由 research（研究、反复搜寻）加 -er（施事者后缀）构成；research 为 re-（反复、加强）加 search（搜寻，经古法语 cerchier 源自拉丁语 circare“巡行、绕行”，词源为 circus“圆圈”），本义为“反复走访以查明问题的人”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of researcher, all circling one idea: a person who searches a subject until the evidence settles. The search may be academic, journalistic, clinical, commercial, independent, archival, or still being learned.
sensesIntro.cn: researcher 的八个义项都围绕一个观念：把一个问题搜寻到证据落定为止的人。这种搜寻可以是学术的、新闻的、临床的、商业的、独立的、档案的，也可以是尚在学习中的。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a document room at midnight, thirty-year-old borrowing cards spread out, a timeline drawn in pencil.
core.cn: 核心意象：午夜的档案室，三十年前的借阅卡摊满桌面，铅笔画出时间线。

branches.en: THE SEARCH ITSELF: systematic inquiry, and the digging out of facts for a report or inquiry.
branches.cn: 搜寻本身：系统探究，以及为报道或调查把事实挖出来。

branches.en: INSTITUTIONAL ROLES: a laboratory or university post, and a clinical investigator with ethical duties.
branches.cn: 机构角色：实验室或大学岗位，以及承担伦理责任的临床研究员。

branches.en: COMMERCIAL SEARCH: surveys and consumer studies aimed at demand rather than natural law.
branches.cn: 商业搜寻：面向需求而非自然规律的问卷与消费者研究。

branches.en: OUTSIDE AND INSIDE THE ARCHIVE: the independent scholar and the close reader of documents.
branches.cn: 档案内外：独立学者，与细读文献的人。

branches.en: THE CRAFT BEING LEARNED: a junior member who researches while still in training.
branches.cn: 正在学习的技艺：一边受训一边做研究的初级成员。

intro.en: Researcher is research plus -er. Research is re- plus search, and the -er suffix marks the person. The family also supplies researchable and researched.
intro.cn: researcher 由 research 加 -er 构成。research 是 re- 加 search，-er 标记人。词族还包括 researchable 与 researched。

latinIntro.en: Latin circus and circare supply the base of search through Old French. The prefix re- is Latin, and the agent suffix -er is native English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 circus 与 circare 经古法语提供了 search 的词基。前缀 re- 来自拉丁语，施事后缀 -er 是英语本族成分。

items.example: The Latin word survives in English circus and in circle.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁词在英语 circus（马戏场）与 circle（圆圈）中留存。

items.example: The verb described going over a district in search of something.
items.exampleCN: 该动词描述为寻找某物而走遍一个区域。

items.example: They searched the attic for the missing deed.
items.exampleCN: 他们在阁楼里寻找那份失踪的地契。

items.meaningCN: 仔细搜寻，后指系统研究
items.example: Her research on the harbour took ten years.
items.exampleCN: 她对这座港口的研究花了十年。

items.meaning: a person who carries out research
items.example: A researcher must record where each figure came from.
items.exampleCN: 研究者必须记录每个数据的来源。

items.meaning: more than one person carrying out research
items.example: Researchers disagree about the date of the wall.
items.exampleCN: 研究者们对这段城墙的年代意见不一。

items.meaning: able to be investigated with available evidence
items.meaningCN: 可研究的；有证据可查的
items.example: The question is interesting but barely researchable.
items.exampleCN: 这个问题很有意思，却几乎无法研究。

items.example: The biography is well researched and clearly written.
items.exampleCN: 这部传记研究扎实，文字清晰。

items.example: The school adopted a research-based reading programme.
items.exampleCN: 学校采用了一套基于研究的阅读课程。

definition_zh: 大量的；相当多的（后接不可数名词，强调分量足以产生影响）
definition_en: a large quantity of something that cannot be counted one by one, enough to matter
core_image: 工地上的沙堆从围栏这头连到那头，卡车来回跑了整个上午
scene: 工地上的沙堆从围栏这头连到那头，卡车来回跑了整个上午才够用。 The site needed a substantial amount of sand before the foundation could be poured.
sceneCN: 这里指沙子的分量极大，足以支撑开工（第 1 个义项：物质数量大且不可数）；句意为在浇筑地基之前，工地需要大量的沙。图中可辨识物件：连成一片的沙堆、围栏、来回运料的卡车。

pos.zh: （固定搭配）大量的；相当多的（后接不可数名词）

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁语「实体」一词进入英语，义为「物质、实质」
由名词加形容词尾构成，义为「大量的、实质的」
由形容词加副词尾构成，义为「很大程度上」
由同一词根加另一形容词尾构成，义为「实质性的」，易与本词混淆
由法语「上升、累计」动词进入英语，义为「数量；总计」

senses.title: A large quantity of material
senses.definition: to have a great deal of a physical substance that is measured in bulk
senses.definitionCN: 指某种按体积或重量计量的物质数量很大
senses.example: The repair needed a substantial amount of cement before the wall could be rebuilt.
senses.exampleCN: 这次维修需要大量水泥，墙才能重建。
senses.why: Amount is for what is measured in bulk, and substantial adds weight to the measure.
senses.whyCN: amount 用于按体积计量的东西，substantial 又给这个度量加上分量。

senses.title: A large quantity of time
senses.definition: to require or consume a great deal of time
senses.definitionCN: 指需要或消耗大量时间
senses.example: The translation took a substantial amount of time because every term had to be checked.
senses.exampleCN: 这项翻译花了大量时间，因为每个术语都要核对。
senses.why: Time is treated as a mass, which is why it takes amount rather than number.
senses.whyCN: 时间被当作整体来量，所以它接 amount 而不是 number。

senses.title: A large sum of money
senses.definition: to involve a great deal of money
senses.definitionCN: 指涉及一大笔钱
senses.example: A substantial amount of money was set aside for the roof repairs.
senses.exampleCN: 为屋顶维修预留了一大笔钱。
senses.why: Money is the most familiar mass noun in the phrase, and the one most likely to be counted in budgets.
senses.whyCN: 金钱是这个短语里最熟悉的不可数名词，也是预算里最常被算的一项。

senses.title: A large quantity of information
senses.definition: to involve a great deal of recorded information
senses.definitionCN: 指涉及大量被记录的信息
senses.example: The survey produced a substantial amount of data that took months to sort.
senses.exampleCN: 这项调查产生了大量数据，整理了好几个月。
senses.why: Data is treated as a mass in careful usage, so the phrase fits reports and archives.
senses.whyCN: 在严谨用法里 data 被当作整体，所以这个短语适用于报告与档案。

senses.title: A large quantity of work
senses.definition: to require a great deal of effort or labour
senses.definitionCN: 指需要付出大量努力或劳动
senses.example: Finishing the index took a substantial amount of work by the whole team.
senses.exampleCN: 完成索引花了整个团队大量工夫。
senses.why: Work is measured by effort rather than by units, which keeps it on the amount side.
senses.whyCN: 工作量按付出而不是按件数来量，所以它留在 amount 这一边。

senses.title: A large body of evidence
senses.definition: to involve many findings taken together as a mass
senses.definitionCN: 指把许多发现合在一起当作一整块
senses.example: A substantial amount of evidence now supports the link between the two events.
senses.exampleCN: 现在有大量证据支持这两个事件之间的联系。
senses.why: Findings are countable one by one, but a body of evidence is treated as a mass, and the phrase follows that habit.
senses.whyCN: 发现本身可以一条条数，但「一批证据」被当成整块，这个短语沿用这一习惯。

senses.title: The countable contrast
senses.definition: to stand opposite a substantial number of, which takes plural count nouns
senses.definitionCN: 指与接可数复数的「数目」类说法相对
senses.example: A substantial amount of grain was stored, while a substantial number of sacks were left empty.
senses.exampleCN: 大量谷物被储存起来，同时大量麻袋被空着留下。
senses.why: The pair splits mass from units, and a writer who mixes them usually reveals a hasty draft.
senses.whyCN: 这一对说法把整体与个体分开，混用的人往往暴露出草稿的仓促。

senses.title: The 'solid' sense of substantial
senses.definition: to be real, solid or important rather than merely large
senses.definitionCN: 指真实、牢固或重要，而不只是数量多
senses.example: The plan needed a substantial amount of support from the council before it could proceed.
senses.exampleCN: 这项计划需要议会相当大的支持才能推进。
senses.why: Substantial began as 'standing under', so its other sense is about having substance, not about bulk alone.
senses.whyCN: substantial 本义是「站在下面」，所以它的另一义讲的是有实体，而不只是量大。

intro.en: Substantial comes from Latin substantia, that which stands under, from sub- and stare, to stand. Amount came through Old French amonter, to go up or mount, from mont, a mountain, and originally meant the total to which things mount up. The quantity phrase is modern; its first date is uncertain.
intro.cn: substantial 出自拉丁语 substantia「站在下面的东西」，由 sub- 与 stare「站立」构成。amount 经古法语 amonter「上升、登上」来自 mont「山」，本义是事物累加所达到的总数。量词短语属现代用法，首见年代不确定。

items.en: Sub- plus stare gave substantia, what stands under a thing and so its substance.
items.cn: sub- 与 stare 合成 substantia，即站在事物下面的东西，也就是它的实体。

items.en: Stare meant to stand, and it supplies the picture of something solid beneath.
items.cn: stare 意为站立，它提供「下面有东西立着」的画面。

items.en: Amonter meant to go up or mount, and English borrowed it as amount.
items.cn: amonter 意为上升、登上，英语借作 amount。

items.en: Mons meant mountain, the image behind the idea of piling up to a total.
items.cn: mons 意为山，是「堆高到某个总数」这一想法背后的画面。

items.en: Substance entered English first, and amount followed as a word for totals.
items.cn: substance 先进入英语，amount 随后作为表示总数的词出现。

items.en: Modern usage keeps amount for mass and number for units, a division that the phrase now depends on.
items.cn: 现代用法让 amount 管整体、number 管个体，这个短语如今就依赖这一分工。

note.en: The first group shares the substance or amount root; the second group names neighbouring quantity phrases.
note.cn: 第一组共享「实体」或「总量」词根；第二组是与它相邻的量词短语。

entries.definition: Physical matter, or the essential point of something.
entries.definitionCN: 指物质，或某事的要点。

entries.definition: To a great degree, or in the main.
entries.definitionCN: 指在很大程度上，或大体上。

entries.definition: Real and important, not merely formal; often confused with substantial.
entries.definitionCN: 指实质而重要的，不只是形式上的；常与「大量」那一形容词混淆。

entries.definition: A total quantity of something measured in bulk.
entries.definitionCN: 指按整体计量的数量。

entries.definition: To climb or increase, from the same mountain image.
entries.definitionCN: 指攀登或增加，同出「山」的画面。

entries.definition: The plainer synonym, with less emphasis on weight.
entries.definitionCN: 指更平实的同义说法，分量感较弱。

entries.definition: A large quantity, phrased as a judgement.
entries.definitionCN: 指很大的量，带判断语气。

entries.definition: A very common spoken equivalent for mass nouns.
entries.definitionCN: 指不可数名词极常见的口语同义说法。

entries.definition: Enough and more, without measuring precisely.
entries.definitionCN: 指足够且有余，不作精确计量。

entries.definition: A large quantity, often of goods.
entries.definitionCN: 指很大的量，多用于货物。

entries.definition: The countable counterpart, used with plural nouns.
entries.definitionCN: 指对应的可数说法，接复数名词。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations keep the 'standing under' picture, the mountain of totals, and the mass-noun rule.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想保留「站在下面」的画面、「堆成山的总数」，以及不可数名词的规则。

normal.en: Sub plus stare is 'stand under', so substantial is what has something solid underneath.
normal.cn: sub 加 stare 是「站在下面」，所以 substantial 就是底下有实在东西。

normal.en: Amount came from a verb meaning to mount up, so a pile of sand is a total that rose like a hill.
normal.cn: amount 出自「往上堆」的动词，所以一堆沙就是像小山一样升起来的总数。

normal.en: Amount takes the uncountable; number takes what you can point at one by one.
normal.cn: amount 接不可数，number 接能一个个指出来的东西。

normal.en: Substantive is the cousin about importance; substantial is usually about size.
normal.cn: substantive 是讲重要性的亲戚，substantial 通常讲大小。

normal.en: A sand pile reaching the fence is the picture to keep for a large quantity.
normal.cn: 一堆沙一直堆到围栏，就是「大量」该记住的画面。

abstract.en: Substance is what remains when the label is removed, and the word still carries that weight.
abstract.cn: 实体是标签去掉后仍留下的东西，这个词仍带着那份重量。

abstract.en: A large amount is a mass you can lean on, not a number you can count.
abstract.cn: 大量是一团可以靠上去的分量，而不是一串可以数的数字。

abstract.en: Enough to matter is the hidden test in the word substantial.
abstract.cn: 「多到足以产生影响」是 substantial 里没有明说的标准。

examples.en: The project required a substantial amount of time and money.
examples.cn: 这个项目需要大量的时间与金钱。

examples.en: A substantial amount of evidence supports the new explanation.
examples.cn: 有大量证据支持这一新解释。

examples.en: A substantial amount of water is lost through the old pipes each year.
examples.cn: 每年有大量水从旧管道中流失。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「阿 色布斯丹夏 阿芒特 奥夫」——沙堆得抵住围栏：大量的

root: substantial 出自拉丁语 substantia「实体」（sub-「在下」+ stare「站立」）；amount 经古法语 amonter「上升、累计」来自 mont「山」（拉丁语 mons）。前者重「有实体」，后者重「累计的量」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all measure bulk: material, time, money, data, work, evidence, the countable contrast and the older sense of solid worth.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在量「整块的分量」：物质、时间、金钱、数据、工作、证据、与可数的对照，以及「有实体」的旧义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sand pile runs from fence to fence after a whole morning of trucks.
core.cn: 核心意象：卡车跑了一上午，沙堆从围栏这头连到那头。

branches.en: THE PILE: a substance is measured in bulk, not in units.
branches.cn: 沙堆：物质按体积量，而不是按件数。

branches.en: THE HOURS AND THE SUM: time passes in a mass, and money is set aside in a heap.
branches.cn: 时辰与款项：时间成块流过，金钱成堆预留。

branches.en: THE DATA AND THE LABOUR: records accumulate, and work is measured by effort.
branches.cn: 数据与劳动：记录堆积，工作按付出计。

branches.en: THE EVIDENCE: many findings are gathered into one body heavy enough to lean on.
branches.cn: 证据：许多发现聚成一块重到可以倚靠的整体。

branches.en: THE COUNT AND THE CORE: number takes units, and substance means there is something solid underneath.
branches.cn: 个体与内核：number 接个体，substance 意味着底下有实在东西。

intro.en: One half means 'standing under' and the other means 'mounting up', and both meet in the idea of something solid and large.
intro.cn: 一半意为「站在下面」，另一半意为「往上堆」，两半都汇入「东西实在且量多」的意思。

latinIntro.en: Latin substantia supplies the first half; Latin mons, by way of French, supplies the second.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 substantia 提供前半，拉丁语 mons 经法语提供后半。

items.exampleCN: 它标出站在事物下面的东西。

items.example: It supplies the solid picture in substantia.
items.exampleCN: 它提供 substantia 里「立住」的画面。

items.example: It is the source of substance and substantial.
items.exampleCN: 它是 substance 与 substantial 的来源。

items.example: It forms substantial.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 substantial。

items.example: It forms substantially.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 substantially。

items.example: It is the image behind amount.
items.exampleCN: 它是 amount 背后的画面。

items.example: It carried the mountain image into English.
items.exampleCN: 它把「山」的画面带进英语。

items.example: It supplies the quantity half of the phrase.
items.exampleCN: 它提供短语中「数量」的一半。

items.example: It forms substantive, the cousin about importance.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 substantive，即讲重要性的亲戚。
